Yet fortified pockets remain in thorned redoubts west of Razor Hill. Gar'Thok, an officer at Razor Hill, leads the effort to remove the remaining Razormane. He sends seasoned defenders into the western bramble camps to kill their scouts, warriors, and dustrunners. Gar'Thok and the Horde leadership fear any quilboar foothold near Razor Hill could bring disaster. They see this strike as the first step toward securing Kalimdor. Once the quilboar defenders are gone, Horde forces can burn the bramble dens and keep the Razormane from reclaiming the western foothills. The fire destroys an enduring menace and secures Durotar's western perimeter. It also protects the vital supply roads between Razor Hill and the wider realm.

quest:8373.text: The Power of Pine. During Hallow’s End, Sergeant Hartman asks you to clear Forsaken stink bombs from Southshore. A pine-scented cleaner helps keep the village clean. During Hallow’s End, the Forsaken foul Southshore with stink bombs. The bombs mar the celebration of liberation. Sergeant Hartman asks you to remove any that have landed in the village with a Stink Bomb Cleaner.

quest:84.text: Back to Billy. Bernice Stonefield sends you across the road with a pork belly pie for Billy Maclure. He has information about her missing necklace, and the delivery carries on the feud between their families in central Elwynn Forest. The feud between the Stonefields and Maclures leaves little room for kindness. Auntie Bernice Stonefield baked a pork belly pie because Billy Maclure would not share what he knew about her family heirloom without one. She hands you the pie with plain irritation. Bernice hopes Billy chokes on every bite.

quest:85.text: Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield looks for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the family across the road, and asks you to find him. The Stonefields and Maclures live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but goodwill between them is scarce. When “Auntie” Bernice Stonefield finds her cherished necklace missing, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain Billy Maclure came onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

quest:8569.text: Past Efforts in Warsong Gulch. In Warsong Gulch, soldiers hold Ashenvale’s southern border while commanders honor their sacrifices. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks steadfast service, even when battle brings no clear victory. Along Ashenvale’s southern border, the Silverwing Sentinels and Warsong Outriders fight brutal skirmishes. Many battles end without a clear victory. Stormwind, Orgrimmar and other capitals honor those who hold their ground against the odds. The Ribbon of Sacrifice marks fighters who gave themselves to the struggle. Far from the front, Alliance Brigadier Generals and Horde Warbringers oversee their forces. Recruiters send new fighters to Warsong Gulch, while quartermasters and tacticians account for veterans returning from hard campaigns. By honoring courage in stalemate or defeat, leaders help keep soldiers committed to holding Ashenvale.

quest:86.text: Pie for Billy. In Elwynn, you gather meat for Bernice's pie while Billy holds back what he knows about her necklace. Bernice agrees to bake, though she believes Billy stole her family's jewelry. Billy Maclure gives no apology when you ask about the necklace. He will neither return it nor name who has it until he gets a freshly baked pork belly pie. He knows Bernice is the finest cook in the valley, and means to enjoy the bargain. Bernice is furious at the thought of feeding the boy she believes stole her family's jewelry. Still, she agrees to bake before you gather the meat. You bring her meat from wild boars roaming nearby pastures. She sets aside her pride, hoping to get her prized necklace back.

quest:860.text:
Sergra Darkthorn. At the Crossroads, Sergra Darkthorn awaits tauren hunters leaving Mulgore behind. Melor Stonehoof sends them north into the Barrens, where danger grows harsher and the Horde's lands reach beyond their home. When their first trials are done, Melor Stonehoof sends young tauren hunters east from Mulgore. Bloodhoof Village and its valleys are familiar ground, where patient tracking has prepared them for what comes next. Now he tells them to pack their gear and cross the mountain pass into the Barrens, leaving their homeland's safety for harsher country. The road winds through red rock canyons before opening onto the Barrens' broad, sun-scorched savanna. There, where Kalimdor's central trade routes meet, the Crossroads is a fortified settlement shared by orcs, trolls, and tauren.

Sergra Darkthorn waits on its eastern side. The experienced orc shaman demands much of the hunters she guides. She teaches those who come to stalk the Barrens' fierce wildlife, testing their eagerness against the discipline the wilderness requires.

quest:861.text: The Hunter's Way. In Mulgore, young adventurers follow The Hunter's Way under Skorn Whitecloud's guidance. You hunt flatland prowlers and take their claws to Melor Stonehoof on Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise, proving your skill and respect for the wild. Among the tauren, hunting is one of the highest honors. It asks for patience, care for the Earth Mother's balance, and respect for the beasts of the plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud tracked across Kalimdor for decades before coming to rest in Mulgore. Seeing young adventurers eager to roam, he gives them a traditional trial to turn ambition into discipline. Flatland prowlers test a candidate's tracking skill. Great cats, they move swiftly and quietly through Mulgore's high grass, then ambush their prey. Bring four sets of claws to show you can find a predator before it finds you. Then turn its own ferocity against it. With the claws gathered, you climb the wooden towers and bridges to Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. Melor Stonehoof receives the trophies there. A master tracker, Melor values Skorn Whitecloud's ancient wisdom. He accepts the claws as proof that you have the spirit to learn more of Kalimdor's hunting ways.

quest:86576.text: Bloodfury Trinkets. Mor'rogal asks you to bring him sunstones from the Bloodfury harpies in the Charred Vale. He says they are bound to the lights of the skies. The Bloodfury harpies gather shiny things, among them golden-yellow sunstones. Mor'rogal is up on the hills above you and has mentioned using them. He asks you to bring him any Glittering Sunstones you find. Mor'rogal says sunstones reflect the sun's majesty. They can adorn shrines and homes with small motes of light. At night, the moon lends them its silver beauty. To him, they recall a bond with the lights of the skies.

quest:86667.text: Snowbound. In Loch Modan, Grenhild studies the local elementals while Norric Lochthane asks for snow from South Gate Pass. His request carries a deeper hope: the aging shaman longs to see his former student again. Grenhild is studying Loch Modan's local elementals when a minor elemental arrives with a message from Norric Lochthane, her former mentor. He urgently needs fresh, unmelted snow for his shamanic workings. Grenhild asks a traveler to fetch it so she can stay with her studies. The snow comes from South Gate Pass, where cold drafts preserve the drifts year-round, and must be sealed in a specially crafted ceramic jar to keep the valley heat at bay. Norric Lochthane lives in a quiet cottage on the Loch's northwest coast, away from the settlements. When the jar arrives, he is pleased to have the cold reagent for his mystical research. Yet he laments that Grenhild did not come herself. His request was for more than a magical ingredient: the aging shaman hoped to reconnect with his former student, now following her own path.

quest:86784.text: Sticks and Bones. Deathguard Bartholomew asks travelers to bring dry branches to Eleanor Shackleton in the western hills of Tirisfal Glades. She camps far from the settlements and knows how to live in the wilds. Between patrols in Tirisfal Glades, Deathguard Bartholomew looks out for Eleanor Shackleton. Deathguards guard against the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders, yet Bartholomew also cares for his acquaintance. Eleanor spends her unlife in the harsh elements, so he asks you to bring dry branches for her campfire. Eleanor Shackleton survives alone in Tirisfal's blighted wilderness. The Forsaken are undead, yet they still feel the damp, bitter chill rolling off the northern moors. Eleanor's rule is simple: when you think you have enough firewood, gather five times more. Grateful for the extra timber, she lets you keep Bartholomew's basket and shares the warmth of her fire.

quest:87.text: Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Billy Maclure's careless play has set the Stonefield and Maclure families against each other. His trail leads you to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt. He says he found the necklace before a creature snatched it away. Billy says a large kobold with gleaming fangs took the shiny necklace and fled to a den above Fargodeep Mine. Yet Goldtooth lurks on the mine's lower level. Slaying the kobold returns Bernice's necklace and settles the families' dispute. Bernice also gives you an old campaign keepsake left by her late husband.

quest:87288.text: Soft Saber Pelts. Across Azeroth, Soft Saber Pelts come from cats that threaten travelers on the roads. Their thick coats make warm blankets and shawls. Saber cats prowl the roads used by couriers, merchants, and lone travelers across Azeroth. People may admire their grace, yet growing numbers near trade routes bring sudden attacks. Hunters keep those roads safe for everyone who depends on them. The hunt yields more than pelts. Frontier camps value saber cats’ dense coats for their warmth and strength. Skilled hands make the pelts into shawls and heavy blankets, giving shelter from harsh weather.

quest:87491.text: Spark of Freedom. The fire elemental has spent its strength in a blazing display. The Dark Irons held its attention, and the rest of the group is relieved it never turned on them. The fire elemental's display leaves the onlooker amazed, then relieved when the creature runs out of strength. The Dark Irons had drawn its attention. Had it turned on the rest of the group, they too could have been in danger.

quest:88.text: Princess Must Die!. At Stonefield Farm, Ma Stonefield asks you to kill Princess before the sow ruins the harvest. The enormous prize-winning pig from Brackwell Pumpkin Patch keeps raiding the Stonefields’ vegetables, putting the family’s crops at risk. The sow belongs to the Brackwells. She grew enormous by crossing onto the Stonefield plots. Ma has had enough of Princess eating the crops she worked to grow. She wants the pig put down before the season’s yield is lost. Princess stays at Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, east beyond the Maclure homestead. Protective boars surround her. Get past her guards and bring Ma the distinctive brass collar from Princess’s neck. It will prove the sow can trouble the Stonefield fields no more.

quest:8827.text: Winter's Presents. In Ironforge, revelers gather for the Feast of Winter Veil. They direct travelers to Greatfather Winter beside the Smokywood Pastures stalls, where gifts wait beneath the holiday tree. Winter settles over Khaz Modan, and Ironforge fills with cheer for the Feast of Winter Veil. Revelers and holiday enthusiasts point passersby toward the decorated tree near the Smokywood Pastures vendors. Smokywood Pastures, a goblin enterprise, shares the season with Greatfather Winter. He greets visitors as goblin merchants remind gift recipients that festive treats and seasonal wares make gifts for friends and family.

quest:8828.text: Winter's Presents. The Feast of Winter Veil brings gifts beneath Orgrimmar’s festive tree. Holiday organizers and goblin apparatus tenders send Horde heroes to Great-father Winter to receive them. Late-year winds sweep across Durotar as Orgrimmar pauses for the Feast of Winter Veil. Promoters from Smokywood Pastures and holiday enthusiasts spread word through the capital that gifts wait beneath the decorated tree. Warriors, hunters, and wanderers resting in the city are invited to share in the season’s generosity. Great-father Winter sits near the Smokywood Pastures market among holiday ribbons and packaged cartons. The ancient figure marks the season’s renewal. Nearby, goblin merchants offer seasonal wares and festive treats to visitors.

quest:886.text: The Barrens Oases. Beneath the Barrens, strange power stirs, and Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem takes heed from Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise. He sends travelers east through Mulgore to meet Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads and investigate the new waters. For generations, the Barrens have known drought while Mulgore flourishes under the Earth Mother's care. Now tauren druids on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise feel strange currents waking beneath the plains. Life stirs where it should not, and the Cenarion Circle fears the power behind it may endanger the land and its creatures. Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem sends Tonga Runetotem to investigate the strange stirrings. The wilderness is too dangerous for one investigator, so Hamuul asks travelers leaving Mulgore to follow. Go east past Bloodhoof Village and through the mountain passes to the Crossroads, where Tonga waits for news. There, in the Barrens, stands the Horde's busy heart.

quest:90902.text: Rediscovering the Light. In Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken paladins learn that the Light still answers them, though it burns. The Holy Light still answers newly risen Forsaken paladins, but it burns their withered bodies. Many once served as champions of the Silver Hand or knights of Lordaeron. Aramis Hammerhand teaches them that powers they once used without thought now bring fierce pain. The Light clashes with the foul magic that sustains undeath, so calling on it takes resolve and endurance. Deathguards in Deathknell suffer grievous wounds fighting mindless zombies, and Forsaken paladins are called to heal them. Aramis teaches that enduring the burning pain is like exercising an atrophied muscle. The paladins bear that agony as a badge of honor and proof that the Light has not forsaken them.

quest:91208.text: Coming to Terms. A frightened former paladin has fled into the hills west of the chapel. Aramis Hammerhand asks a newly risen knight to reach her with compassion. The Silver Hand's former paladins wake among the Forsaken in shock. In life, they served the Holy Light and fought the undead. Now their souls are bound to decomposing flesh. Aramis Hammerhand guides some through this change, while others flee into the Tirisfal wilderness, unable to face their new existence.

quest:91209.text: Continue Your Training. In Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken paladins begin their training before setting out for Brill. Aramis Hammerhand sends them east through Tirisfal Glades, where danger and distrust greet those who wield the Holy Light. After learning martial combat and channeling holy power in Deathknell's graveyard, you travel east through Tirisfal Glades to Brill. The town is the regional outpost and administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the training of those who follow the paladin's path in undeath. Aramis warns that an undead paladin's calling is perilous. Lordaeron still needs defenders against threats from beyond, yet wielding the Holy Light under Sylvanas Windrunner's banner invites suspicion. Many Forsaken suffered agony or death at the hands of holy zealots. Among their undead kin, the Light's presence breeds distrust.

quest:91285.text: Murlocs at the Gates. Breton Samuels asks you to drive back murlocs troubling the keep. Their attacks make rebuilding harder. Murlocs still trouble the keep after you and the others drove them from their spawning grounds. Their attacks are growing harder to manage, so Breton Samuels asks you to drive back some of them. They lurk in the bluffs along the eastern road and in camps around the lake to the west. Breton Samuels expects the attacks to continue. He hopes pushing back the Vile Fin attackers and seers will slow them down. The keep is already hard to rebuild while murlocs strike at its people.

quest:91294.text: Touring the Grounds. Breton asks you to walk Bandarion Keep after the murloc attacks come under control. Meeting Danitha Morr is your first step toward settling among the residents. Breton asks you to meet Bandarion Keep’s residents and look around the stronghold. Once you have finished, Danitha Morr can help you settle in. The keep is still small, but its people call it home. Danitha Morr introduces herself as the closest thing Bandarion Keep has to a commander. She welcomes those seeking fellowship with people still loyal to the Light. The keep needs help before it can be fully established.

quest:91316.text: Making Repairs. At the fortress, a shortage of building materials has made restoration difficult. You are sent to Shadowvale to search for lumber. Shadowvale is a ruined village in the Whispering Forest, southwest of the fortress. Search an old root cellar in one of its buildings for usable materials. The fortress lies far from settled lands, so bringing in supplies is difficult. Its repairs depend on what can be found there.

quest:91317.text: The Tarnished. At Shadowvale in Tirisfal Glades, the Tarnished threaten a fledgling order's place among the Forsaken. Their attacks deepen mistrust and put the order's future at risk. Some risen still bear prejudices from their former lives, and now attack their fellow Forsaken. The Tarnished have gathered at Shadowvale, southwest of here. Their violence must end, and Commander Rudolph Gelhardt’s head must be brought back. The Tarnished’s attacks give those who distrust the order more reason to turn against it. Stopping them may help the order earn a place among the Forsaken. Acceptance could still take years or decades.

quest:916.text: Webwood Venom. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker studies the giant webwood spiders of Shadowthread Cave. He asks young night elves for venom sacs to learn how Teldrassil's growth has affected the forest's wildlife. Gilshalan Windwalker has come to Shadowglen to study the webwood spiders in Shadowthread Cave. They are far larger and more aggressive than their cousins elsewhere. He suspects Teldrassil's immense magical energies are changing the local wildlife. So he asks for venom sacs to compare with those of ordinary spiders and learn what has changed. Webwood spiders live in and around Shadowthread Cave, where they threaten young night elves in the glen. Gathering their venom can help thin their numbers. It also gives Darnassian researchers evidence of Teldrassil's effect on the wild.

quest:917.text: Webwood Egg. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker seeks a Webwood Egg for his study of Teldrassil’s wildlife. Venom samples are in hand, but he needs a living specimen to study the unnatural aggression in the forest’s creatures. An egg can be examined safely, without capturing a full-grown spider. Gilshalan Windwalker needs living subjects to understand the unnatural corruption affecting Webwood spiders around Shadowglen. You have gathered venom from the aggressive spiders, but taking a thrashing giant from the depths could prove deadly for a novice. So Gilshalan asks you to bring an unhatched egg from the brooding clutches inside Shadowthread Cave. Webwood spiders brood in Shadowthread Cave, where the increasingly hostile arachnids make their nests. An intact egg gives scholars a subject they can hatch under containment. Gilshalan plans to send it to Darnassus with his venom samples for examination. With his local study complete, he directs recruits toward higher duties in the boughs of Aldrassil.

quest:91723.text: Delicate Instruments. Hamish Bergwort's instruments at the Tower of Azora falter as surges of magic rise from the north. Their source is Jasperlode Mine, where kobold geomancers stir the earth. At the Tower of Azora, Hamish Bergwort's arcane apparatus needs careful calibration. Uncontrolled surges keep unsettling his measurements. He cannot make precise adjustments while the interference continues. The magical pulses lead north to Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have taken its tunnels, where their geomancers work crude earth magic. Their frequent rituals send ripples through the stone. Those tremors unsettle the Tower of Azora's sensitive instruments.

quest:91724.text: Delicate Instruments. At the Tower of Azora, Defias magic troubles Delicate Instruments. Hamish Bergwort's equipment suffers from erratic spellcasting near Stone Cairn Lake. The disturbance must end before his instruments can work properly. Hamish Bergwort studies arcane questions in the Tower of Azora. His work depends on precise readings, and even a slight change in local magic can ruin hours of careful study. He suspects crude spells nearby are causing the interruptions. Defias rogue wizards practice magic near Stone Cairn Lake, and their casting causes the interference. Their unchecked spellcraft brings unstable magic into Elwynn. End their casting, and the disturbance will cease, allowing Bergwort's instruments to give clean readings.

quest:91725.text: Stolen Enchanting Supplies. Near the Tower of Azora, Blixie Fitzwink has lost the supplies she was carrying after a gnoll ambush. The enchanting reagents are scattered among camps around Stone Cairn Lake. Their return could spare her weeks of chore duty and keep Master Theocritus's arcane studies supplied. Blixie Fitzwink was carrying supplies from a trading post to the Tower of Azora when gnolls ambushed her on the road. She fled, leaving the cargo scattered among their camps along Stone Cairn Lake. The valuable reagents were meant for Master Theocritus, whom Blixie assists. Now she asks travelers to recover them, fearing weeks of cleanup duty after her arcane polymorph experiments. Master Theocritus conducts sensitive magical research at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. His work depends on delicate reagents brought from local trading posts. Gnoll packs around Stone Cairn Lake have grown bolder, making the route dangerous. The lost supplies could interrupt his studies, while their return may spare his beleaguered assistant further trouble.

quest:91732.text: Good Steel. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Hagar Lowe seeks good steel for the tools worn by its woodcutters. With fine metal scarce after the wars, he sends adventurers to Jasperlode Mine for picks whose steel can be reused. After the wars that battered the human kingdoms, good steel grows scarce in Elwynn Forest. At Eastvale Logging Camp, woodcutters rely on sturdy axes, saws, and other tools. Constant use and poor metal have worn them down. Without steady shipments from Stormwind's foundries, craftsman Hagar Lowe must keep the camp working with what he can find. North of Eastvale Logging Camp, Jasperlode Mine lies abandoned after its fall. Miners once worked its rich veins with finely made picks, forged when steel was plentiful and expertly tempered. Hagar sends adventurers into the infested tunnels to bring those picks back to Eastvale. Their sound metal can be melted down and made into tools for the camp's lumberjacks.

quest:91733.text: Downstream. Near Eastvale Logging Camp, Ormin Pelford's wagon has overturned, and the river has carried his woodworking tools downstream. Murlocs and wolves guard the banks where they lie. Laborer Ormin Pelford was bringing a shipment back from a local trading post when his wagon tipped near Eastvale Logging Camp. Its gear spilled into the river, and the current swept it downstream before he could secure it. Without the woodworking tools, the loggers face delays in their timber work. Ormin Pelford's lost cargo lies along banks where murlocs and wolves roam. Aggressive murlocs claim the muddy shoals downstream, while predatory wolves prowl the surrounding woods. Ormin cannot face those dangers alone. He needs hardy travelers to search the riverbanks, recover the submerged saw, axe, and toolbox, and bring them back safely.

quest:91736.text: Applejack Still. At the Applejack Still, cider becomes a clear, potent spirit. Apple vapor rises as the coils turn it into liquor. Fermented cider passes through the still and emerges as strong spirit. Near the apparatus, apple vapor stings the nostrils. Pipes and coils draw the fruit's essence and condense it into liquor. Alcohol vapor condenses inside the still and becomes a clear spirit. Applejack flows from the outlet into a waiting bottle, ready to drink or store. Even in rough field conditions, the apparatus produces a clear, potent brew.

quest:91740.text:
Croaky's Head. At Ridgepoint Tower, Croaky's death brings grim relief to a grieving Stormwind garrison. The murloc leader terrorized eastern Elwynn's roads. Proof of his death gives the guards hope as they struggle to secure the waterways. Murlocs along Elwynn Forest's rivers and streams have grown bolder. They ambush travelers and threaten trade routes. Croaky was a particularly aggressive chieftain who rallied other murlocs to attack near local roads. Merchants, farmers, and travelers between Elwynn and Redridge now face deadly roads. Croaky's death ends his ambushes and removes a threat to Stormwind's hold on the eastern woodland outskirts. Ridgepoint Tower guards Elwynn Forest's eastern edge and the strategic crossing into the Redridge Mountains. Officer Merell Ross leads the guards, though dangers around the outpost have stretched them thin. Murloc attacks recently killed two watchmen on patrol.

The deaths shook the garrison and exposed the vulnerable border. Bringing Croaky's severed head to Ross proves the chieftain is dead. Now the guards have reason to hope they can drive the raiders back from Elwynn's borders.

quest:91741.text: Nibbled-On Book. In Northshire Valley, Nibbled-On Book has been chewed by kobolds. Brother Paxton hopes to see it returned to Northshire Abbey's modest collection. Kobolds in Northshire Valley scavenge what they find left unguarded. You recover a chewed tome from a slain kobold, its cover torn and its parchment marked by teeth. The book came from the library shelves of nearby Northshire Abbey. Valley kobolds have been taking volumes from there. Brother Paxton tends the small library inside Northshire Abbey, where the Brotherhood of Northshire reads and studies. Kobolds from the valley slip inside and snatch books from the shelves. Paxton is grateful to have this nibbled volume back. Yet he worries about the rest of his collection still missing in kobold hands.

quest:91743.text: Rascally Rodents. Kobolds are carrying books away from Brother Paxton’s library in Northshire Valley. He fears they are devouring the abbey’s collection. Brother Paxton fears the kobolds that have spread from the hills and mines into Northshire Valley’s sacred grounds. He believes they are devouring books from his collection. With the library at risk, he asks young adventurers to hunt the kobolds and recover whatever volumes they can.

quest:91745.text: Mining Consultant. At Echo Ridge Mine, Kelsey Fargo watches the kobolds from her post outside the entrance. Their strange movements have drawn local attention. Kobold trouble at Echo Ridge Mine has taken an odd turn. The creatures defend their underground claims and gather candles, but now their coordinated disturbances have caught the authorities’ attention. You are sent to Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed near the entrance. From her post outside the tunnels, she has watched the kobolds closely.

quest:91746.text: Elmpaw's Head. At Elmpaw's Head, the hunt is over, and a wealthy collector awaits its prize. The beast’s head goes to a handler who prepares and mounts trophies for affluent patrons. Elmpaw has fallen, and hunters prize the beast’s head as proof of victory. Trackers regard the hunt as an impressive feat, a hard-won end to the chase. A handler rewards you for Elmpaw’s severed head. Then the handler prepares and mounts it for wealthy patrons who want fierce wild trophies on their mantles.

quest:91751.text: Rough Wolf Pelts. Near Goldshire, Rough Wolf Pelts are needed for Helene Peltskinner's leather orders. Her husband is occupied near Northshire Abbey, so she asks for help skinning local wolves. Just outside Goldshire, Helene Peltskinner supplies travelers and residents with cured leather and furs. Her husband usually hunts Elwynn Forest's timber wolves for her. Now his duties near Northshire Abbey keep him away, while customer orders wait. So Helene asks passing apprentices to skin the local wolves. Timber wolves prowl Elwynn Forest's woodlands, farmlands, and roads. Skinning them gives novice skinners practice harvesting hides. Their pelts help Helene continue her leatherwork and keep trade moving through Goldshire. Hunters, too, sharpen their woodcraft.

quest:91752.text: The Big Picture. In Northshire Valley, kobolds carry stolen illustrated books into the mine for Shinyfinder Narf. The volumes are to be returned to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey. Kobolds in Northshire Valley have been seen fleeing with books and crying, “Picture for Narf!” Most gather candles and shiny trinkets, but Shinyfinder Narf seeks illustrated tomes. He has collected a sack of them in his hideout beneath the mine.

quest:91753.text: An Enchanting Lesson. At the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, Kitta Firewind gives An Enchanting Lesson to apprentice enchanters. Kobold geomancers bind simple magic into crude wax effigies, showing why practice matters alongside arcane theory. Kitta Firewind, an enchanter at the Tower of Azora, challenges apprentice enchanters to look beyond polished libraries. She asks them to examine magic where it appears naturally. Even the uneducated kobolds beneath Elwynn Forest channel cantrips into everyday talismans, proof that magical instinct can thrive without formal schooling. Kobold geomancers shape Crude Wax Effigies with simple folk enchantments. Students obtain the effigies and carefully unravel their bound magic through disenchantment, extracting Luminous Residue. By taking these primitive charms apart, they learn how raw magic behaves in the field. Enchantment's fundamental threads are found through observation as well as in grimoires.

quest:91758.text: Follow That Kobold!. A kobold has fled Northshire's mines with Brother Paxton's books, and the abbey calls on Tordrin Sternblade to track it. Follow That Kobold! begins with a theft from the local mines. Kelsey saw a kobold flee the Northshire Abbey mine tunnels with a heavy sack of books. The workers and clerics thought the vermin in the mines were under control. The books belong to Brother Paxton, who needs them back in the abbey's collection. The kobold is a nimble scavenger from below ground. Tracking it through Northshire Abbey's wooded grounds calls for special skill. You are sent behind the abbey to the stables, where Tordrin Sternblade can be found. The dwarven Hunter trainer has newly arrived from Ironforge, and his wilderness knowledge can help pick up the kobold's scent.

quest:91772.text: Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds. Kobolds are moving from Northshire Valley toward Elwynn Forest. You follow their trail with a tracking kit and report what you find to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire. Kobolds have spread beyond Northshire Valley and the abbey grounds. With a tracking kit, you follow their trail to learn where they gather. Your report will help Goldshire prepare for threats across Elwynn Forest.

quest:91775.text: Book Return. In Elwynn, Marshal Dughan sends you to Fargodeep Mine for Brother Paxton’s lost books. One volume, “Fun with Elementals,” could place dangerous instructions in kobold hands. Marshal Dughan sends you into Fargodeep Mine for books belonging to Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey. Kobolds have overrun the mine, and Paxton fears they might read “Fun with Elementals.” Its simple instructions could teach them to summon an elemental in the tunnels. Fargodeep Mine once brought gold to the kingdom of Stormwind. Now kobolds overrun its lower levels, while Elwynn’s defenders are stretched thin. The damp, dangerous caverns threaten the books. You carry the recovered volumes in a protective book bag, keeping Paxton’s records safe and arcane lessons beyond the kobolds’ reach.

quest:91777.text: Rare Books. In Northshire Valley, Rare Books sends you after two primers taken by kobolds. Brother Paxton needs them back at Northshire Abbey. Brother Paxton has lost two books from the library at Northshire Abbey. Kobolds carrying books and other things have taken them into Jasperlode Mine. The missing volumes are Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards and Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words. Both are primers on magic.

quest:918.text: Timberling Seeds. At Lake Al'Ameth, botanist Denalan studies the growing hostility of Teldrassil's nature elementals. He seeks Timberling Seeds to test whether enriched soil can help them grow calmer. His work joins the quiet efforts of night elf herbalists to understand the subtle afflictions troubling the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to Teldrassil's boughs, bound closely to the health of the surrounding flora. Usually they reflect the forest's balance in peaceful form. Their recent hostility alarms the local night elves, though no cause is known. Botanist Denalan seeks to learn what stirred them before choosing to cull them. Denalan suspects the blemish lies deep in the ground. He hopes to raise a gentler generation of timberlings in enriched, carefully treated loam. By gathering seeds from wandering timberlings near Lake Al'Ameth, he will test whether the land's corruption can be countered from the roots up.

quest:91899.text: A Sealed Crate. Trade handlers seek lost cargo as bandits disrupt the roads. You can recover sealed crates from the wilderness and outlaw camps to help keep supplies moving. Highway crime has risen of late. Organized bandits and rogue thieves prey on trade routes, ambushing wagons, pack trains, and lone couriers. Their cargo is scattered across wilderness roads or carried off to outlaw camps. These raids threaten the supply lines between settlements. Traders and cargo handlers rely on independent adventurers to recover lost freight and keep supplies moving. Sealed crates rescued from bandits or found abandoned in the brush can be brought to trade handlers. There, the goods help secure supplies, curb illicit trade, and restore safety to regional commerce.

quest:919.text: Timberling Sprouts. Around Lake Al'Ameth, Timberling Sprouts are spreading across Teldrassil. Denalan asks you to uproot them before they grow into hostile timberlings. Corrupted sprouts spread along Lake Al'Ameth's banks. Denalan lives beside the lake and knows these young plants cannot be healed. Left alone, they quickly become aggressive, bark-covered timberlings that threaten wildlife and travelers. Uprooting them helps protect the grove. Denalan is troubled by how quickly new sprouts appear across Teldrassil. Their spread points to sickness in the World Tree's roots and soil. Denalan and the druids of Darnassus seek its cause.

quest:91900.text: A Sealed Crate. Bandits and thieves are raiding the roads, and lost shipments lie scattered across the wilds. Local merchants will pay you to bring a sealed crate back. Caravans and couriers now face ambushes along the old trade highways. Many leave wagons and crates behind when they flee, and the goods sit in the brush until someone finds them. Merchants and depot keepers depend on travelers to bring that cargo home. Carry a sealed crate to a receiving depot and you earn a bounty on the spot. Handlers sort the freight and send it on its way, so commerce keeps moving despite the brigands. While the roads stay contested, lost cargo remains steady work for any traveler passing through.

quest:91904.text: A Sealed Crate. Trade caravans lose sealed crates to thieves along the roads. Merchants seek the missing goods and pay to have them returned, restoring regional supplies. Bandits and thieves strike trade caravans on roads and shipping lanes. Haulers and couriers can lose their shipments in an ambush, leaving sealed crates beside wild roads and paths until someone finds them. Merchants and supply coordinators pay for merchandise returned safely. Bring recovered crates to regional collection points, and the goods can flow through disrupted supply lines again. You are paid for protecting trade.

quest:91905.text: A Sealed Crate. Trade recipients seek A Sealed Crate after bandits disrupt the roads. Recovered cargo helps keep local stores supplied and out of outlaw hands. Bandits and thieves have struck established trade routes, leaving merchant cargo scattered. Their ambushes put caravans and supply lines at risk. Across contested lands, lost shipments are a common sight. Recovering the crates helps local trade endure the lawlessness. Merchants and handlers rely on couriers to bring lost goods back to storage depots. Each returned crate adds to local stores and denies outlaws the gains of highway robbery. In return, salvage workers receive fair pay for facing dangerous roads.

quest:920.text: Tenaron's Summons. In Shadowglen, Gilshalan Windwalker sends you to meet Tenaron Stormgrip in Aldrassil. Your work against dangers in the woods has brought the elder's attention. Your fight against venomous spiders and corrupted wildlife has reached Tenaron Stormgrip. Gilshalan Windwalker tells you the elder wants to see you. Even night elves know better than to keep an elder waiting atop Aldrassil. Tenaron waits in Aldrassil's highest chamber and looks across Shadowglen's boughs. His concerns reach beyond the glen, to Teldrassil's moonwells and the corruption spreading through the young World Tree's ecosystem.

quest:921.text: Crown of the Earth. At Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip prepares young night elves for their departure from Shadowglen. They draw sacred water in a rite that recalls Mount Hyjal and the immortality their people surrendered there. Before young night elves leave Shadowglen, their elders teach them what their people lost. At Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei sacrificed the World Tree Nordrassil to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. The blast took their ageless immortality and sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip teaches this history through a rite, so the novices leave with humility and purpose in a changing world. You draw water from the moonwell north of Aldrassil with a crystal phial. Moonwell waters bear remnants of the ancient Well of Eternity. Druids channel their restorative power into the wild, while Sentinels honor the wells as tranquil shrines to Elune. The kaldorei remain wary of arcane sorcery, which is forbidden. The wellspring sustains their land, yet recalls the reckless magic that nearly broke the world.

quest:92110.text: My First Real Potion. A child asks you to bring murloc eyes for My First Real Potion. She is eager to mix it herself. The child is glad to see the murloc eyes. While you were away, she gathered more herbs and found empty vials downstairs. Now she asks you to mix the ingredients as she watches. The potion turns sickly orange when the eyes go in.

quest:92124.text: Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton needs help finding missing books. He sends young adventurers to Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, to count the library's archives. But Daniel's thoughts turn to local tradeskills, making a clear answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey keeps scholarly works, spiritual writings, and records of Stormwind's history that survived the First War. Brother Paxton, a careful monk, takes pride in the collection. Now books are missing from the shelves, and he needs a clear count to learn how many are gone. He has little patience for chasing his daydreaming helper. Daniel assists Brother Paxton in the abbey library, but his thoughts stray from parchment and catalog numbers. He is fascinated by the practical trades and professions of Elwynn Forest, including smithing, leatherworking, tailoring, and herbal craft. So when Paxton asks him to count the books, Daniel rambles about local crafters instead of looking for lost scriptures.

quest:922.text: Rellian Greenspyre. At Denalan’s retreat by Lake Al’Ameth, you carry a timberling seed to Rellian Greenspyre in Darnassus. The handoff brings word of trouble spreading through Teldrassil’s boughs. Denalan has studied the plants and elemental life around Lake Al’Ameth. After you gather seeds from nearby timberlings, he sends you to Darnassus with one for his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian is a druid who walks the Cenarion Enclave’s terraces. He has taken an interest in Denalan’s research and hopes to grow a timberling of his own.

quest:923.text: Tumors. In Darnassus, the Cenarion Circle works to contain the sickness spreading through Teldrassil. You are sent to Wellspring Lake to gather mossy tumors from afflicted timberlings, so druids can study the poison and burn the growths safely. A strange affliction is twisting Teldrassil’s native plants and animals. Its timberlings, usually placid nature spirits with bark for skin, have grown hostile and erratic. Grotesque mossy tumors spread across their living wood and pulse with unnatural poison. Cenarion scholars Denalan and Rellian Greenspyre search for the cause. Timberlings already lost to the sickness must be culled to protect the rest of the boughs. Wellspring Lake in northern Teldrassil has become a focal point of the outbreak. Its timberlings are among the most tainted on the World Tree. Rellian Greenspyre asks you to kill these corrupted guardians and cut away their tumors. Bring the growths to the druids in Darnassus, where they can be burned safely. The night elves hope this will slow the contagion while they search for the disease’s source.

quest:92457.text: Starving Arcane. Archmage Modera asks you to clear rogue elementals from the City of Dalaran. A breach has unsettled the city's enchantments and defenses, and the Kirin Tor needs room to tend its wards. Walk Dalaran's streets and the damage shows. The breach has disturbed factotums and enchantments across the city, some of them part of its defenses, and the arcane energy they shed now drifts free. It has drawn Seeking Remnants, Saturated Remnants and Mana Echoes, which gather to fill themselves on the loose magic. Each one you put down leaves less of that magic for the next to feed on.

quest:92458.text: Heart of Disruption. The Image of Archmage Modera needs help containing an arcane disruption in Dalaran. The Violet Citadel’s wards are under strain, and the Kirin Tor need time to bring the crisis under control. At the top of the Violet Citadel, a thunderous crash sounded from the parlors. The disturbance began there, and rampant arcane power now threatens the wards. The Kirin Tor are occupied inside, so you receive a key and are asked to find a less public way into the city before the disruption worsens. Modera asks you to collect an Arcane Mote. She does not ask what you saw in the citadel. Her concern is containing the mote and ending the disruption. The Kirin Tor must now take up that work while the wards hold.

quest:92460.text: Coming of Age. In Thendal Village, young Skyborne begin the rite that welcomes them into service to the shen'dorei. Ailee Farheart leads them to Rorian the Dayseeker, who gives each initiate an ancestral relic and hears their pledge to aid their people. Ailee Farheart guides young Skyborne from Thendal Village toward adulthood. They travel just west to the greatfather tree, where the village elder waits. For the shen'dorei, the rite marks a passage into adulthood and a pledge to serve their community. Local troubles are rising. At the entrance to the greatfather tree, Rorian the Dayseeker leads the ceremony. He gives each initiate an ancestral relic, an heirloom passed through generations of shen'dorei. The relic is a token of the winds of home. It stays with its bearer until their ashes are scattered to the breeze.

quest:92461.text: Harmony in Balance. On Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker gives fledgling adventurers an early rite of duty. You thin the vuldren in Thendal Grove to protect the island’s natural balance, for its beasts feel magic shifting in the winds. In Thendal Grove, vuldren have grown too numerous for the island to sustain. Their numbers threaten the environmental harmony that supports Zephras Isle’s wildlife. Rorian the Dayseeker gives young protectors the duty of thinning the herd before it strains the grove and the life around it. Vuldren are usually docile, yet the beasts of Zephras Isle are sensitive to the island’s atmosphere. When magic carried on the winds falls out of balance, they respond sharply. Keeping their numbers in check helps prevent them from becoming unpredictable and dangerous pests.

quest:92462.text: Infestation Investigation. In Thendal Grove, cirrusflies swarm the eastern woods. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight sends young defenders to thin their growing numbers before nearby settlements are at risk. Local rangers report a sudden rise in cirrusflies along Thendal Grove’s eastern edge. One is a minor pest, but a swarm grows aggressive and destructive. So Ranger Elatrell Featherlight sends capable youths to cull the insects before they overwhelm the grove. After coming of age, young defenders help keep Zephras Isle safe. Clearing pests protects nearby settlements from outbreaks in the woods. Yet entrails and insects clinging to returning hunters show the swarm is far larger than first feared.

quest:92463.text: The Cirrusfly Queen. In Thendal Grove, cirrusflies threaten the rangers of Zephras Isle. Their swarm has spread far, so Elatrell Featherlight sends you to hunt its queen and thin the flies at their source. You have seen that killing worker cirrusflies does little to curb the swarm spreading through Thendal Grove. Elatrell Featherlight sends you to the grove’s southeastern reaches, where the main hive lies. The queen directs the colony and heavier soldier drones guard her. From afar, cirrusflies may seem like petty pests. Yet the larger breeds threaten anyone who passes beneath Zephras’s boughs. Hunt down the matriarch and withstand her guards, and you prove your skill in battle. Featherlight’s rangers will give you praise and respect.

quest:92464.text: Elemental Unrest. Near the Thendal Standing Stones, lesser wind spirits have grown restless. Their sentient elemental benefactors have departed Zephras Isle, and Rorian the Dayseeker sends you into Thendal Grove to find his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, and learn what troubles the breeze. For generations, powerful wind spirits lived beside the people of Zephras. They were sentient, and they guided and protected the islanders. Now those elemental benefactors have departed, leaving Zephras in lasting imbalance. Without them to tend the air, simple sprites reflect the volatile feelings and forces that linger across the land. Northeast of Rorian's post, the air near the ancient Thendal Standing Stones has turned hostile. The lesser wind spirits lack true self-awareness, so they act in reaction, not malice. Rorian sent his apprentice, Yala Windwatcher, to watch their erratic behavior from the grove's edge. She is to discover what unseen tension disturbs them.

quest:92465.text:
Agitators. On Zephras Isle, unrest in Thendal Grove draws Yala Windwatcher's concern. The Al'Aketh cult has stirred peaceful wind sprites into hostile elementals, and its converts now threaten the grove. Cultists of Al'Aketh have pushed into Thendal Grove and stirred the wind spirits who dwell there. Once peaceful, the sprites now rage as roiling winds, threatening anyone who passes through. Yala Windwatcher asks you to subdue the enraged elementals and the Al'Aketh converts behind the unrest. Quieting the wind creatures may restore a fragile calm to the grove.

Yala grieves at the thought of shen'dorei blood shed among her own people. Yet while the cult remains, she sees little choice.

quest:92466.text: Call of Earth. Initiates gather what their instructor asks of them in Call of Earth. Their effort shows whether they are ready to continue their training. An initiate faces a test of resolve when the instructor asks for particular materials. The gathering tests patience and endurance. By meeting the earth’s demands, the student shows the strength needed to commune with its enduring power. When the initiate returns with the requested offerings, the instructor sees their grit. The student has held firm through the trial and is ready for the next step in spiritual training.

quest:92467.text: Call of Earth. At the Rise of Spirits, you drink an Earth Sapta and meet an elemental guide. The earth's strength may help you seek the winds again. Shamans drink saptas to open their sight to the elemental world. Each brew attunes a mortal spirit to one realm and reveals spirits usually hidden from view. Only those with enough resolve can bear their power. Select practitioners guard the knowledge of these brews. You travel northeast through a pass to the Rise of Spirits, where initiates commune with the earth. Saptas are drunk only at sacred sites. On consecrated ground, the draught lets you pierce the veil and see what the spirits choose to reveal.

quest:92468.text: Call of Earth. An earth spirit sends you to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove with a shard of Rough Quartz. There, the shard becomes the heart of your first Earth Totem and begins your study of the elemental forces. An earth spirit gives you a shard of Rough Quartz as proof of your communion. It sends you to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove with the shard. Even the smallest fragment can endure. The spirits grant favor and respect to those who show patience, resilience, and wisdom. Windshaper Boros sets the Rough Quartz at the heart of your Earth Totem. He reminds you that the elemental path has four parts. You may long to hear and sing the songs of the wind. Yet mastery begins with understanding all four forces, starting with the unyielding ground beneath your feet.

quest:92469.text: Return to Rorian. Yala Windwatcher sends you to Thendal Grove with urgent news from the field. After you help drive back the agitators on Zephras Isle, she reports that the Al'Aketh have disturbed the local wind spirits. Yala Windwatcher remains on Zephras Isle to face the hostiles still there. She sends you to Thendal Grove with word that the Al'Aketh are no longer working only in the shadows.

quest:92470.text: Foul Matriarch. In the caves south of Thendal Village, Aetheen of the Gales tests new initiates against the ursera. They must thin the packs and slay their den mother, Urs'anah, to prove they can face greater perils across Zephras Isle. Around Thendal Village, Aetheen of the Gales watches newcomers find their footing. When an initiate shows early skill, Aetheen sends them into the southern caves for a dangerous rite of passage. There, they thin the local ursera packs and face the broodmother who threatens the village's edge. Local rangers know the ursera are fierce, but Urs'anah is the greatest threat to the haven. Deep in Thendal Cave, the formidable matriarch directs her scavengers and guards her lair. Her severed head proves an adventurer can face ferocious beasts and is ready to venture beyond the starting grove.

quest:92471.text: Aetheen of the Gales. On Zephras Isle, young adventurers who pass their first trials go to meet Aetheen of the Gales at Thendal Grove. There, the next generation faces her judgment. Young novices on Zephras Isle take on early duties that test their grit and spirit. The island's mentors watch for those ready to help defend their home. Rorian the Dayseeker notices youths prepared for greater responsibility. At Thendal Grove, Aetheen of the Gales reads the currents of the air. She belongs to the Council of Elders, which governs Zephras Isle, and assesses young shen'dorei as they come of age. Reporting to her takes you beyond minor duties along the island's perimeter and toward threats facing the community.

quest:92472.text: The Next Step. Elder Aetheen turns south after the beasts near Thendal Village are dealt with. The Al'Aketh Cult's zealots threaten Shen'dar Village. Elder Aetheen of the Gales sees danger growing across Zephras Isle. The predators and matriarchs of the northern wilderness have been dealt with, but that was only the lesser trouble. Outlying settlements still need defenders. The Al'Aketh Cult is the chief danger in southern Zephras. Its ruthless zealots worship Al'Akir the Windlord, ruler of Skywall in the elemental realm. Their growing power threatens Shen'dar Village. Aetheen sends travelers south along the road, past ambushers in the highlands, to aid Constable Aonda's local guard.

quest:92473.text: Aggressive Encroachment. At the village, starving ursera now threaten the settlement. Valreaa Valewind calls for a cull after one beast nearly attacked a child at the elder tree. Ursera from dens southwest of the village have become dangerous to its people. A hungry adolescent reached the base of the central elder tree and nearly mauled a child at play. The settlement's rangers killed the beast before anyone was hurt. The rangers believe hunger is driving ursera toward settled ground. They have ordered a cull of the scrawniest beasts prowling outside their dens in Thendal Grove. The Rangers of the Grove hope this will stop further incursions while they seek the cause of the wildlife's distress.

quest:92474.text: Falling With Style. At Thendal Village, Myriaal Mistwake sends young Skyborne from a watchtower to test their falling skill. They glide down to Rorian the Dayseeker below. High above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage with a daring leap. She urges newcomers to step from the watchtower ledge and trust their gift for slowing a fall. The practice is playful, yet it prepares them to walk on air when danger comes beyond the grove. Myriaal delights in sudden descents that startle onlookers, while Rorian the Dayseeker favors caution. As novices glide down to land before him, he warns that careless use of their magic may leave travelers helpless in danger. Still, he accepts that controlled practice within the village has its place.

quest:92479.text: A Scribbled Letter. At Northshire Abbey, adventurers receive a summons from Tordrin Stemblade after clashes with nearby kobolds. It calls promising recruits to seek his training as Stormwind faces growing dangers. After clashes with kobold camps in the valley, adventurers at Northshire Abbey receive a hasty letter sealed by Tordrin Stemblade. It asks them to give it prompt attention before taking up other business. The summons brings budding champions to formal mentorship within the abbey’s protective grounds. Tordrin Stemblade says times have changed. Unfamiliar folk now take up weapons to defend the realm. As the wilderness around Northshire grows more dangerous by the day, he offers travelers counsel day or night. He guides them as they master their skills and help Stormwind’s beleaguered people.

quest:92481.text: A Student of the Arcane. On Zephras Isle, Rorian the Dayseeker calls novice spellcasters to A Student of the Arcane. After newcomers prove their mettle, they review a Glowing Recall Crystal and report to Dorii Brightwhisper, the local mentor. After helping with the troublesome vuldren near Thendal Grove, fledgling mages receive a curious artifact: a Glowing Recall Crystal. Dorii Brightwhisper, the island’s arcane instructor, left it behind. Its recorded message tests an initiate’s aptitude and welcomes them into deeper study of magic. Dorii Brightwhisper says arcane mastery has slowly faded among their people. For millennia, they lived secluded high in the clouds. So Dorii sees each new practitioner as a pioneer who can recover lost knowledge and restore their people’s once-mighty magical heritage.

quest:92482.text: The Way of the Hunter. Young hunters in Thendal Grove begin training after driving back the local vuldren. Now Rorian the Dayseeker summons them to meet Tai'ree Farsight and begin formal tutelage. After thinning the disruptive vuldren on Thendal Grove's outskirts, young hunters return to find their practical skills have drawn attention. Rorian the Dayseeker gives them a scribbled summons from Tai'ree Farsight, the grove's resident hunter trainer. For novice rangers preparing to explore Zephras Isle, the meeting turns their work from defending the island to learning martial skills and survival. Near the center of the village, Tai'ree Farsight welcomes promising pupils with stern realism. Thriving in untamed nature demands sharp senses and lightning reflexes. Her guidance comes from her long years of experience, giving island trackers a foundation for honing their marksmanship and survival skills.

quest:92483.text: At Home in the Shadows. Rorian sends you to meet Akeri Duskblade in Thendal Grove, where rogue training begins. The summons marks a change from village chores to stealth and combat. Akeri Duskblade has noticed young rogues dealing with threats around Thendal Grove. The grove's rogue trainer avoids an open meeting in the settlement, so he sends a note through Rorian the Dayseeker. Though Akeri keeps his reasons close, Rorian sees that he knows the skills a rogue needs beyond the grove's sheltered bounds. Akeri Duskblade waits in the Thendal Grove village watchtower. He judges each newcomer’s footing and awareness, then warns that careless steps beyond the grove can lead to an early grave. Passing his scrutiny begins formal training in stealth, precision, and survival on Zephras Isle.

quest:92484.text: Embracing the Elements. In Thendal Grove, Rorian the Dayseeker calls young shamans to begin their elemental training. Windshaper Boro’s message speaks of a silence between the people and the spirits of the winds. Rorian the Dayseeker comes to you after you help with the vuldren around the village. Windshaper Boro left a humming recall crystal while you were away. Its message calls you to the center of the grove, where formal elemental instruction begins. Windshaper Boro tells you the spirits of the four winds ended all communication years ago. They left behind the communion they once shared with the people. Now the shamans of Zephras study the natural world and train hard, hoping to bridge the silence and speak with the spirits again.

quest:92485.text: A Student of Nature. On Zephras Isle, A Student of Nature begins with a summons to novice druids. After they help restore local harmony, Xyton Silverwind calls them beneath the boughs of Thendal Grove to learn the isle's natural balance. After local disturbances caused by overzealous wildlife are resolved, Rorian the Dayseeker brings a personal summons to young initiates. The folded parchment was left by Xyton Silverwind. It invites aspiring druids to step forward and study the deeper mysteries of the wild, for their natural talents have caught the grove elders' attention. Meeting Xyton Silverwind on the lower level of the great tree in Thendal Grove marks a novice's first step in their calling. To Silverwind, Zephras Isle's plants and animals form an intricate living whole that needs constant care and watchful balance. The path of fang, claw, feather, and branch calls for lasting mentorship, and this meeting begins a lifetime of stewardship.

quest:92489.text: Power Overwhelming. High Sorcerer Andromath sends aid from Stormwind to Dalaran, where arcane power has turned dangerous. The Kirin Tor rebuild behind closed borders, and a Mana Elemental threatens their work. After Archimonde destroyed Dalaran in the Third War, the Kirin Tor drew inward. Scholars and sorcerers once came from across the world to its doors. Now the surviving magi keep outsiders away as they rebuild their ruined city behind closed borders. As the Kirin Tor restore Dalaran, arcane energy has grown dangerous. Volatile leaks surge out of control and take shape as beings of pure mana. High Sorcerer Andromath fears internal turmoil could undo the city’s recovery, or that Dalaran could abandon its old ties to the Alliance. So he sends champions from Stormwind to quell the Mana Elemental and remind the Kirin Tor that their allies still stand with them.

quest:92514.text: Welcome to Shen'dar Village. At Shen'dar Village, newcomers are sent to meet its elder and innkeeper. Local tensions share the frontier with a growing bandit threat. Newcomers in Shen'dar Village first meet the people who guide daily life there. Those touched by the spirits are directed to Elder Illaya Amberwind near the village square. Coriella Calmbreeze welcomes visitors at the village inn, where lodging and supplies are available. These introductions help travelers learn the village's customs before they take up arms. Disputes in Shen'dar Village stay civil, though the Windshapers and the High Order disagree. Their ideological friction runs through the region, but both groups know survival comes first. Bandits are pressing into the area. That danger gives the village reason to set smaller quarrels aside.

quest:92515.text: The Problem With Prideclaws. The Shen'dar Highlands village faces danger from prideclaws, bandits, and cultists. The beasts press toward the settlement, and culling them guards the people while providing useful pelts. Prideclaws are pressing toward the village in the Shen'dar Highlands. Bandits roam the hills, and unhinged cultists trouble the region. Villagers face danger from several sides. As the beasts grow bolder and their territory spreads, the settlement draws nearer to their reach. Villagers have organized a culling before the wandering predators can snatch pets or children. Driving prideclaws back from the borders helps guard the settlement. Their sturdy pelts also give village craftsmen material for useful goods.

quest:92516.text:
Hippogryph Harassment. Near Shen'dar Village, Hippogryph Harassment puts travelers in danger. A wild flock nests southeast of the village in the Shen'dar Highlands and attacks those on the nearby road. You are asked to cull its young, protectors, and matriarch so travelers can pass safely. Travelers near Shen'dar Village face danger from the skies. A wild flock nests southeast of the settlement, in the Shen'dar Highlands. Across Kalimdor, hippogryphs are known as noble beasts, and some are bonded to elven riders. Untamed flocks, though, fiercely guard their territory.

Wagons and lone travelers on the paths below have become targets of aerial ambushes. The attacks disrupt passage and could leave the village isolated if the creatures go unchecked. The flock's nesting grounds in the Shen'dar Highlands must be confronted to end the danger. To make the high roads safe, kill the young before they reach maturity and overcome the vigilant protectors guarding the perimeter.

The matriarch directs attacks on passersby. Travelers can use the roads safely again only when the nest is struck and she is felled.

quest:92517.text: The Criminal Element. The Highlands Bandits terrorize the Shen'dar Highlands from a cave behind a waterfall. A new cult has arrived, and local defenders are stretched thin. So outside help is needed against the gang's leader, "Badwind" Bennic. The Highlands Bandits have made their den in a hidden cave behind a northern waterfall in the Shen'dar Highlands. Their leader, "Badwind" Bennic, commands cutthroats who troubled the locals long before an enigmatic cult arrived. Since then, their lawlessness has grown into terror. Local defenders are stretched thin and cannot spare forces, so you are sent to break the gang and bring Bennic down.

quest:92528.text: Among the Faithful. At Falaath Village, you pass among the Faithful of Al'Akir in the Shen'dar Highlands. Their growing ranks and storm magic draw close scrutiny, while their leaders gather with plans that threaten nearby settlements and outposts. You enter Falaath Village in the Shen'dar Highlands as an eager recruit among the Faithful of Al'Akir. The cultists boast that their ranks are growing. They claim their devotion gives the storm its shape and fury. New arrivals are usually sent to Skypriest Aanders for scrutiny, but an unexpected meeting at the village inn interrupts that routine.

quest:92529.text: Falaath Village. At Falaath Village, marked recruits gather to seek the Windlord's favor. They come from Shen'dar Village to report to Missionary Jasaan and join the faithful. In Shen'dar Village, Sania Silverstream says her people grew prideful and took the bounty of the air for granted. The wind spirits abandoned them, and stagnation followed. Now penitent recruits receive the Mark of Akir and travel to Falaath Village. There, they join others who hope their acts of contrition will restore the wind's favor. At Falaath Village, Missionary Jasaan welcomes initiates bearing the Mark of Akir. Jasaan sees each new acolyte as a blessing from the four winds. Those who arrive may seek the elemental grace of Al'Akir.

quest:92532.text:
The Warrior's Path. Rorian the Dayseeker sends you to Blademaster Ren in Thendal Village. She offers young warriors instruction and discipline to defend their people. After restoring balance nearby, you return to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Village. The village blademaster has noticed you, and Rorian gives you a crumpled note written by Ren herself. She asks you to come to her directly.

Ren waits in the village watchtower, high above the settlement. From there, she watches the island's borders and the recruits who may one day defend them. Inside the watchtower, Blademaster Ren teaches you that combat takes more than brute strength. A warrior must lead, endure, and protect as the world grows more uncertain. Ren pledges to guide you as you hone your skills. Her rigorous training prepares you for the greater dangers threatening your home.

quest:92544.text: Al'Aketh Thugs. At the temple ruins near Thendal Grove, Al'Aketh cultists threaten travelers. Sent from the Shrine of Akir under High Priestess Lorthuna's orders, they harass wayfarers and force recruits into their ranks. Hanaa Nightwind asks you to break their hold and slay their commander. Just southwest of Thendal Grove, ancient temple ruins have become dangerous for travelers. The Al'Aketh have seized the grounds and prey on people near the grove. Rangers stationed nearby suspect High Priestess Lorthuna sent the ruffians from the Shrine of Akir. They bully the people and force them to submit to the cult. At the ruins, Malduko Cloudcrush rules through violence and fear. Brutes and newly indoctrinated neophytes obey him, making the temple an aggressive outpost at Thendal Grove's doorstep. Hanaa Nightwind hopes that striking down Cloudcrush and scattering his followers will break the cult's confidence. It will warn them that coercion will not be tolerated in these lands.

quest:92550.text: Havoc in the Highlands. In the highlands, Shen'dar Village moves against Al'Aketh forces at Falaath Village. Its defenders mean to stop an assault before it begins and protect their home. Zealous cultists are preparing to assault Shen'dar Village. So its leaders send you into the ruins of Falaath Village to strike first, before the Al'Aketh forces can begin their attack. Al'Aketh zealots gather at Falaath Village and wield chaotic elemental power. You break their ranks by defeating Al'Aketh Stormcallers and shattering Living Lightning. Then you find Commander Cyclas and behead him.

quest:92551.text: Stolen Supplies. Caravans bound for the Shen'dar Highlands are under attack, and their stolen goods gather in Falaath Village. Food and windstones grow scarce in the highland settlements, leaving some skyborne close to starvation. For months, raiders have attacked caravans on the road between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands. Their wagons carry food and windstones that highland settlements depend on. As fewer deliveries arrive, townsfolk struggle to get by, and some draw close to starvation. The Al'Aketh blame common bandits for the attacks. Yet the missing supplies keep turning up in Falaath Village, where the Al'Aketh store the stolen packs. The recovered goods go to the local authorities and constable, who send them straight to the skyborne in greatest need.

quest:92553.text: Restocking the Larders. In the Shen'dar Highlands of Zephras, a village cook needs help keeping the food stores full. Danger keeps the villagers from foraging, so the cook turns to you for eggs and strider meat. Rising dangers make life harder in the Shen'dar Highlands. Villagers can no longer safely enter the wilderness to forage or hunt, and the communal stores are nearly empty. So local cooks rely on travelers willing to brave the wild trails and help keep the settlement fed. The cook asks you to find strider meat and fresh small eggs among the highlands' wildlife. In return, the cook shares knowledge of local game and its recipes. Small eggs fried in ursera tallow offer comfort, with dried peacebloom for a quiet pipe.

quest:92579.text: To Valanaar. Aonda sends an urgent report across the island to Valanaar, where the peacekeepers prepare for a growing threat. Their leader, Valennia Stormfist, must ready her people as conflict with the cult draws near. After you help defend Shen'dar and its pylon, Aonda entrusts you with urgent word for Valennia Stormfist. Valanaar lies at the island's southeastern edge, where the peacekeepers keep their headquarters under Valennia's command. Aonda warns that the peaceful days are ending. Valennia must prepare her people for an inevitable clash with the aggressive, expanding cult.

quest:92595.text: The Windshapers. Among the wind spirits, The Windshapers seek a way to keep Zephras and the Shen'dorei alive. Illaya Amberwind welcomes new recruits to their work, as dangers gather in Skywall. Illaya Amberwind welcomes new recruits into the Windshapers, who commune with the wind spirits and protect the Shen'dorei. The order seeks those born with spiritual perception. They hope to mend the growing rift between their people and the elemental forces that sustain their aerial realm. Every Windshaper bears that burden. The Al'Aketh bring turmoil within Skywall, and the elemental plane holds dangers of its own. The Windshapers believe Zephras can endure and the Shen'dorei can weather the storm only if they restore their bond with the spirits of the winds.

quest:92596.text: The High Order. On Zephras, Rathiril Sunlance tells newcomers why the shen'dorei must now stand alone. Their elemental benefactors are gone, so these Highborne descendants of Eldre'Thalas turn to ancient arcane magic to protect their people. The shen'dorei on Zephras are working to reclaim their strength and choose their own path. For a long time, elemental benefactors protected them. Now those patrons are gone, leaving the people exposed to strife within and dangers around them. Rathiril Sunlance seeks those gifted in arcane magic to help preserve their people and build their strength on their own. The shen'dorei carry the legacy of Eldre'Thalas and an innate wellspring of arcane energy. Even those never formally trained in wizardry share that power. The High Order sees it as the destiny of Highborne descendants to wield these ancient gifts. With them, the shen'dorei hope to resist the Al'Aketh within and face the many threats to their home on Zephras.

quest:92597.text: Reading the Ley Lines. On Zephras Isle, young Skyborne seek the arcane currents beneath their feet. Falorne Fallwind sends them to Thendal Grove to feel power rising through the elemental plane. Ley lines run beneath Zephras Isle, even through the elemental plane. Strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh cross the island as these buried currents rise toward the surface. For those with the bloodline and knowledge to channel them, the exposed lines open a path to raw arcane power. Falorne Fallwind urges initiates to claim their Highborne ancestry instead of seeking favor from wind spirits. The local Windshapers and the Al'Aketh both look to such spirits. Fallwind believes survival amid the elemental plane's harsh powers depends on mastering the arcane force beneath the ground, rather than asking foreign creatures for mercy. Northeast of the settlement, Thendal Grove's ancient standing stones mark a powerful meeting of ley lines. Roiling winds and Al'Aketh converts surround this exposed place. There, initiates can attune their senses to the ley line's pulse and unleash the full potential of their natural racial abilities.

quest:92598.text: The Gift of Skysight. On Zephras Isle, Ventaari Brightwish guides young Windshapers toward Skysight. At an Elemental Convergence, they awaken their perception and listen to the spirits. Windshapers are born with a bond to the elemental forces that shape their world. They call its sacred faculty Skysight. This gift attunes mortal senses to the spiritual realm and reaches across the divide between the living and the unseen. In the wilds, a Windshaper can call on this inner vision. Near concentrated power, the bond grows stronger, bringing boons and wisdom whispered by the spirits. Northeast of the settlement, ancient standing stones mark an Elemental Convergence in Thendal Grove. Raw energies gather at such places, where spirits linger. Ventaari Brightwish sends novices there to test their spiritual strength. Skysight grows with practice, like a faculty of body or mind. Windshapers must learn to read the elements' changing omens, for their people's survival depends on it.

quest:9260.text: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Lieutenant Orrin calls Stormwind's defenders to drive back Scourge forces pressing against the city. Necropolises loom beyond its walls, and he asks them to gather Necrotic Stones and study the runes around enemy camps. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital. Glowing runes mark the dirt around Scourge camps, but their purpose remains unclear. The circles crackle with magic like that of the necropolises and carry eerie whispers. Lieutenant Orrin can only guess who, if anyone, hears those unnatural voices.

quest:9261.text: Investigate the Scourge of Ironforge. The Scourge presses against Ironforge’s gates, and Lieutenant Nevell calls for defenders. Undead troops gather beneath a hovering necropolis while glowing runic circles mark their camps. Lieutenant Nevell and the Argent Dawn watch the undead at Ironforge’s mountain entrance. Necropolises hover above Dun Morogh’s frigid heights, far from Lordaeron and the plagued lands of the north. They mean to stop the Scourge before it reaches the Bronzebeard fortress.

quest:9262.text: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. At Darnassus, Lieutenant Beitha calls for help as Scourge encampments press close. The Argent Dawn needs defenders to strike the undead and learn what the runes outside the gates are for. The Scourge has reached Teldrassil. Floating necropolises loom over invasion camps near Darnassus, and ghouls, skeletons, and other undead horrors spill from them. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn coordinates the city's defense. She calls on volunteers to slow the attack and gather information before the undead overwhelm the night elven homeland.

quest:9263.text: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. Outside Orgrimmar, the Scourge presses its attack beneath a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel calls on defenders to repel the undead, recover necrotic stones, and examine runic circles charged with necromantic energy. The assault brings the Lich King's reach to Durotar. The Scourge now threatens lands far from Lordaeron and the northern ice. Its floating necropolises cast shadows across Azeroth, even over Durotar. Undead forces have gathered at Orgrimmar's threshold and raised camps that threaten the Horde capital. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn coordinate the defense, calling on local champions to drive the invaders back before they can secure a siege.

quest:92679.text: Blood Tithe. In Valanaar, Alvarion Windfield seeks aid for the orchard that sustains his family. Pain keeps the Skyborne farmer from his work, so he sends travelers west to his wife, Aamelia, who tends their lowland farm. Alvarion Windfield has come from his homestead to Valanaar in search of capable fighters. Pain leaves him visibly injured, and he fears for the livelihood his farm provides. He asks you to travel west into the lowlands, where his wife Aamelia tends their family orchard. The Windfield Orchard lies in the lowlands west of Valanaar. Alvarion is too ill to tend the farm, so Aamelia Windfield bears its burdens alone. Reach the western valley, learn what threatens the orchard, and lend the family your strength.

quest:92682.text: Make Yourself Useful. At Windfield Orchard, Ferauu's bandits are taking stormapples before their share is due. Some hungry outlaws have broken ranks to pick the trees early. Drive them off, and the orchard keeper will respect you. Windfield Orchard gives Ferauu's bandits a regular share of its fruit harvest. Ferauu leads the crew, but some outlaws cannot wait for his scheduled visit. They slip into the orchard early to pick stormapples for themselves. The orchard caretaker puts ambitious newcomers to work before Ferauu arrives. The keeper asks you to secure the ripe stormapples and drive off hungry bandits trespassing among the trees. They have gone behind Ferauu's back to take his share. The keeper says Ferauu would likely execute them for it.

quest:92683.text: Flutterfly Dust. In the Gustberry Lowlands, Flutterfly Dust draws a homesteader's interest. Travelers gather it from giant flutterflies while bandits threaten anyone who ventures alone into the fields. Giant flutterflies drift through the outer fields and orchards of the Gustberry Lowlands. Their wings shed fine dust, and you can gather it in bulk. Nearby homesteaders want the powder for practical household needs. Yet the insects remain wild. A Flutterfly Swatter brings dust down with a blunt strike. Most flutterflies panic, take to the air, and shake loose piles of powder. Some turn and strike back when provoked. Usually, they are docile. The dust is messy to gather and clings to clothing and gear for weeks. The homesteader eagerly awaits its delivery, since bandits make solo trips into the fields too dangerous. Ask what the powder is for, and the resident offers only vague words about general stuff and things.

quest:92684.text: Ornery Ornery Galestriders. In the Gustberry Lowlands, an orchard farmer's poor harvest is under threat from galestriders raiding the stormapples. Drive off the boldest birds to save the remaining fruit and bring home tenderloins for dinner. A poor harvest has left Gustberry Lowlands farmers with little to spare. Now wild galestriders strip ripe stormapples from orchard branches and threaten what fruit remains. The farmer needs the boldest birds driven off or culled before the crop is gone. Lowlands galestriders are larger and more bad-tempered than their highland kin. Take care near these towering birds, traveler; one powerful kick can badly hurt or kill a fighter. Their tenderloins give hungry locals a rare, substantial meal.
