quest:92685.text: The Hills Have Eyes. Aamelia faces a bandit assault in the Gustberry Lowlands, and Ferauu’s raid draws near. She sends travelers to strike a camp in the northern hills before the bandits gather. Aamelia faces an approaching attack in the Gustberry Lowlands. Ferauu leads the outlaws threatening her farm. She asks you to strike their camp in the hills to the north. Thin the highwaymen’s ranks before they gather, and Aamelia hopes to weaken their attack and gain time before they arrive.

quest:92693.text: Standing Our Ground. Aamelia Windfield gives you one last chance to retreat to Valanaar before the bandits close in. You have helped the local defenders prepare, yet the coming fight still seems doomed. Aamelia Windfield gives you one last chance to return safely to Valanaar. You have helped the local defenders prepare for the bandits, but the fight ahead looks grim. Will you stand with them, or leave before the clash?

quest:92698.text: What Is My Purpose?. In the orchard fields, a Malfunctioning Cyclone Construct wanders without purpose. Its broken speech has repeated for decades, since the wind elementals departed. Aamelia Windfield knows what locals remember of its past. A Malfunctioning Cyclone Construct paces through the fields, caught in a broken loop. Muffled fragments come from beneath its armor, repeating errors and questions about its purpose. Decades alone have left its old instructions corrupted or forgotten. It looks imposing, but threatens no one who passes. Its broken voice carries over the soil as it wanders without purpose. Aamelia Windfield says the construct has roamed the fields for decades, apparently since the wind elementals departed. Alvarion guessed it once hauled harvests to distant markets or tended livestock, centuries ago, before the land became an orchard. The Windshapers built and maintained cyclone constructs in earlier ages. Orchard workers have talked of asking them to repair the machine, but the matter has never seemed urgent. So it continues to roam, largely ignored.

quest:92699.text: The Supreme Magister. In Valanaar, Elaadrin Evengale draws new arrivals toward the High Order. From a lodge in the settlement’s southeast, the order seeks allies as it faces hostile Windshapers and a nearby cult. New arrivals of promise in Valanaar are directed to the High Order. Supreme Magister Elaadrin Evengale leads it from a lodge in the settlement’s far southeast. He watches newcomers closely, seeking the strength, resolve, and arcane aura to face the dangers threatening their home. Peace in Valanaar is fragile. The High Order and the Windshapers are bitter enemies, so newcomers are warned to keep their distance from the Windshapers lest violence break out in the streets. A dangerous cult lurks nearby. With threats outside the town, its leaders cannot afford bloodshed within.

quest:92700.text: The Grand Skyseer. In Valanaar, the Windshapers seek travelers gifted with spiritual sight. They send you to Ayessa Dawnsinger at their lodge, while rivalries and a threatening cult strain the settlement. You arrive in Valanaar and are sent to the central lodge. There, the Windshapers gather beneath Grand Skyseer Ayessa Dawnsinger. Elder Amberwind has heard of your deeds in Shen'dar Village and welcomes you among those attuned to the spirits. Dangers press from beyond the town and within it, so tread carefully through its fragile politics. Peace in Valanaar hangs by a thread. The Windshapers and the High Order openly oppose one another, and street skirmishes threaten the settlement. A shadowy cult also menaces the region. Local leaders have ordered both factions to keep their distance and face this shared danger instead of fighting over territory. Grand Skyseer Ayessa Dawnsinger says skysight is growing rare among the people of Zephras. Those who arrive with a strong aura and harmony with the spirits are vital allies. The Windshapers need them as they guide their land through hard times.

quest:92701.text: To Valanaar. At Valanaar, Valennia Stormfist must face the cult's growing threat. Aonda sends urgent news from Shen'dar, where the village and its pylon were defended. After Shen'dar and its pylon were defended, Aonda sends a trusted messenger across the island. The message is bound for Valanaar on the island's southeastern edge. There, the commander of the peacekeepers must hear how quickly the cult is advancing. Valennia Stormfist and her peacekeepers have long tried to avoid open conflict with the cult spreading across the island. Yet the events at Shen'dar mark a change. The cult's influence is growing, and Valennia can no longer hold back from a clash. Her dwindling force must ready Valanaar for an assault.

quest:92703.text: Deliver the News. At the Windfield orchard, Aamelia sends word that her family is safe. Alvarion waits in Valanaar, where he went to seek help. Aamelia thanks you for saving the Windfield family orchard. Her home is safe, but Alvarion Windfield has gone to Valanaar to plead for help. He needs to know his family and home are out of danger. Alvarion Windfield is overcome with emotion when you tell him his family and home are safe. He went to Valanaar believing his search for help was a desperate, nearly vain hope. Your success recalls the legendary heroes his people remembered from before they arrived in Skywall. The Windfield family welcomes you into their home for good.

quest:92709.text: A Grand Adventure. In Valanaar, Elaadrin Evengale asks you to hear the High Order’s plans. Their search for ancient magic may shape Zephras Isle’s future. Elaadrin speaks of your Highborne lineage and the young people who may help save their home. The High Order seeks the ancient magic of its forebears, and what has been lost over many millennia.

quest:92727.text: The Missing Scholar. Fillion Flamebreeze is missing after setting out to study atmospheric magic on Zephras. The High Order sent the scholar toward the Shen'dar Highlands, and concern grows as the road from Valanaar yields no word of his return. The High Order gathers and preserves knowledge across Zephras. Yet field research on the island has grown perilous. Fillion Flamebreeze set out for the Shen'dar Highlands to study atmospheric arcane phenomena, but never reported back. His peers now fear the dangers along the frontier roads have claimed him.

quest:928.text: Crown of the Earth. In Shadowglen, you carry moonwell water south to Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. The journey takes you from sheltered training into the wider work of protecting Teldrassil. You have tasted the enchanted water of Shadowglen's moonwell. At the crown of Aldrassil, Tenaron Stormgrip seals the gathered water in a larger vessel and sends you beyond the sheltered glade. The road runs south to Dolanaar, through woods where danger has grown harder to predict. Dolanaar is the first major village beyond Shadowglen, along the cobblestone paths through central Teldrassil. Its moonwell lies at the village's heart. Corithras Moonrage, an elder who oversees preservation across the boughs, waits there. The vessel you carry joins you to the wider effort to protect the World Tree.

quest:92849.text: The Missing Scholar. You follow the trail of Fillion Flamebreeze, missing after an assignment at the Overlook Standing Stones. The search leads north to a cave, where he was dragged by a winged beast. You find signs of trouble along the trail Fillion Flamebreeze took on his travels. They point to foul play. Following them leads north to a dark cave. The missing scholar may still be alive inside, waiting for help.

quest:92850.text: The Missing Scholar. Fillion Flamebreeze is stranded near a dangerous den, and Valanaar needs the threat ended. Once he can travel, he asks you to slay the Shriekling Matriarch nearby. After his ordeal, Fillion Flamebreeze can travel back toward the safety of Valanaar. Yet a brood of shrieklings has nested close to the settlement. Fillion asks you to enter the Shriekling Den and slay the Shriekling Matriarch before the beasts threaten the town.

quest:92871.text: In Service of Zephras. Across Zephras, the Al'Aketh cult is gathering for a wider conflict. The Windshapers send an emissary to assure Valennia Stormfist that they will aid her peacekeepers. Reports of Al'Aketh activity are spreading across Zephras. Valennia Stormfist's peacekeepers have guarded the island for a long while, but the cult now seems to be preparing for a larger conflict. So the Windshapers pledge to stand with Valanaar's forces if open fighting begins. You are sent to Valennia Stormfist to assure her that the Windshapers are ready to aid her peacekeepers. Valennia welcomes their swift pledge. She is ready to speak with you about the cult's worsening threat.

quest:929.text:
Crown of the Earth. Near Starbreeze Village, you draw sacred water for Darnassus. Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar sends young night elves to replenish the city's moonwell and teaches them why their people tend Teldrassil's great boughs. Druids have made you a jade phial for the journey to Starbreeze Village. There, a lesser moonwell holds sanctified water. The phial's refined craft lets you draw the luminous water and carry it without disturbing its purity.

Darnassus's central moonwell depends on scattered fonts like this one. Elders send initiates on foot to keep the city's fountains full of Elune's grace. The journey teaches the young what it takes to nourish Teldrassil. Corithras Moonrage tells you of the sorrow that followed the Battle of Mount Hyjal. The night elves sacrificed Nordrassil, their ancestral World Tree, and lost their immortality. Illidan Stormrage was unleashed amid the ruin, while Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage disappeared.

Grief and isolation marked the days that followed. The kaldorei turned to Teldrassil.

quest:930.text: The Glowing Fruit. A strange fruit shines among Teldrassil's trees, and its growth troubles those who find it. You carry it to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, where the herbalist can study the unfamiliar plant. In Teldrassil's misty boughs, you may find plants bearing large, round fruit that shine with their own light. The World Tree's balance is delicate, and its wildlife has behaved strangely of late. So unusual plants call for care. You gather the glowing fruit to bring it to someone who knows the wild flora.

quest:93036.text: Infiltrating the Cult. In Shen'dar Village, Sania Silverstream draws followers as its uneasy peace begins to fray. The village asks a newcomer to approach her and learn what the Order of the Al'Aketh intends for the settlement. In Shen'dar Village, an uneasy truce with the Order of the Al'Aketh is starting to unravel. Local authorities have long tolerated Sania Silverstream, a self-proclaimed missionary living among them. The Order claims to be a peaceful religious movement and sends gentle recruiters to draw in unsuspecting followers. Village leaders let Sania recruit to keep the cult from open conflict. Now that fragile peace is wearing thin.

quest:93089.text: What Comes Next. On Zephras Isle, the High Order seeks your blessing before departing with its Kirin Tor allies. Their expedition depends on finding an arcane answer to the island’s instability. High Elder Shadowsong has blessed the expedition, and its preparations are ready. Ansirem has worked to establish skycutter travel between Dalaran and Zephras Isle. Now the vanguard is preparing to depart. Speak with Elaadrin Evengale when you are ready to leave the island.

quest:931.text: The Shimmering Frond. A curious plant shimmers among Teldrassil's roots and canopy. Travelers carry a cutting to Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth, hoping the botanist can explain where it came from. A strange plant catches the light in Teldrassil's boughs. Its fronds twist with a pulsing shimmer unlike the island's usual foliage. The glow draws the eye among the young forest's plants.

quest:932.text: Twisted Hatred. Near Teldrassil’s settlements, Lord Melenas has rallied the grell at Fel Rock. Tallonkai Swiftroot sends trusted champions to stop the satyr before he threatens the night elves. Satyrs carry an ancient betrayal in kaldorei history. During the War of the Ancients, they were Highborne who gave themselves to the Burning Legion. Now one has taken hold on Teldrassil, the young World Tree meant as a sanctuary. For Tallonkai Swiftroot and the defenders who stand with him, that presence is a bitter disgrace. North of the nearby paths, Fel Rock’s corrupted caverns crawl with feral grell. Lord Melenas has gathered the chaotic creatures into a hostile force under his will. Tallonkai fears what the satyr may unleash upon the World Tree’s boughs, and demands a swift, quiet end. He wants Melenas slain and his severed head brought back.

quest:933.text: Crown of the Earth. At the Pools of Arlithrien, Corithras Moonrage asks you to fetch water as Gnarlpine furbolgs turn violent. His account of Teldrassil begins with Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance after the Third War. Corithras Moonrage gives you a tourmaline phial and sends you to a moonwell southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the Pools of Arlithrien. The Gnarlpine furbolgs were once peaceful, but now they lash out without warning. They ambush travelers and harry Sentinel patrols across the region. These skirmishes have become a threat to the night elves' new home. When you return with the filled phial, Corithras tells you how Teldrassil began. After the Third War, Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage vanished, leaving the Cenarion druids without a leader and divided. Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm took the mantle of leadership in his absence. He urged the Circle of Ancients in Darkshore to set aside their mourning. The night elves, he argued, had to regain their lost immortality and heal their civilization by planting a vast new World Tree.

quest:93317.text: Crab Season. On Zephras, foragers hurry to gather Windsong crawlers before the brief season ends. Cultists have made the shores perilous, so locals call for help. For a few weeks each year, Windsong crawlers appear along Windsong Lake’s freshwater shores and the rivers that feed it. Their meat is a rare harvest, but the season soon passes. Cultists patrol the wilderness around Zephras, putting local foragers in danger. The journey to Windsong Lake is too hazardous for gatherers alone. Unless you brave the shores and the ill-tempered crabs, this brief harvest may be lost.

quest:93318.text: WANTED: Vulgara the Insatiable. In the Shen'dar Highlands, Vulgara the Insatiable terrorizes travelers and nearby settlements. Constable Aonda has called for a Peacekeeper bounty, with Vulgara's head to be brought to Danarii Bellowveil. Constable Aonda has named Vulgara the Insatiable an immediate danger to the highlands. The massive winged vuldren roosts southwest of Shen'dar Village, where she terrorizes travelers and local settlements. The Peacekeepers call on bounty hunters to end the threat. Bandits and a shadowy cult trouble the Peacekeepers across the region. Slaying Vulgara would ease the danger to local people and keep the skies over Shen'dar safe. Then the defenders could focus on civil defense.

quest:93319.text: Pilfered Windstones. On Zephras, stolen windstones have left emergency stores short. The Highlands Bandits took them while Aonda's few peacekeepers guard against growing cultist numbers at Falaath Village. Windstones keep daily life moving on Zephras. Each settlement keeps emergency stores for times of crisis, but village supplies began to run short. Then captured bandits from the northern Shen'dar Highlands were found carrying the stones. For months, the Highlands Bandits had slipped into local stockpiles, taking what they could while security was thin. Aonda is responsible for village defense, and has refused to approve a raid on the northern cave. The settlement has too few peacekeepers to spare. To the south, cultists are multiplying at Falaath Village, so the guards must hold their posts against that threat. With the peacekeepers pinned down, independent adventurers must face the bandits and recover the stolen windstones.

quest:93461.text: Welcome to Shen'dar Village. In Shen'dar Village, newcomers with Highborne blood are welcomed under a fragile truce. The High Order and Windshapers keep peace within the settlement, while old rivalries simmer beyond its borders. Newcomers with traces of Highborne blood go to the main lodge to pay respects to Rathiril Sunlance, elder of the High Order. They also seek a room from Coriella Calmbreeze, the local innkeeper. Different elven factions share this haven, but their truce remains tense. Daily life brings rooms and odd jobs, yet friction persists between the High Order and the Windshapers. In the village square, both groups observe civility. Beyond the settlement, away from prying eyes, old rivalries go unchecked.

quest:93552.text: Harvesting Windstones. At Thendal Grove, Dalia the Collector asks you to gather raw windstones before their power fades. The ancient elemental energies of Zephras Isle are slowly dwindling. Zephras Isle still draws on wind magic, but its natural defenses are failing. Centuries ago, the wind elementals who shared the island with its elves vanished. Since then, the magic that sustains the land and its great anchor pylons has weakened. So Thendal Grove’s residents need every reserve of raw energy they can secure. Blue crystalline windstones lie scattered through Thendal Grove. Their brittle shells hold dense wind magic from ages past. They cannot sustain the island forever, yet they give its elves a dependable source of arcane power. Gathering raw clusters remains vital to daily life.

quest:93735.text: The Broken Construct. In Valanaar, a damaged construct threatens one of the island’s last working relics. Riaani Nightwind has gone to the city’s western edge to examine it. The old machines carry a history reaching back to the spirits of the wind. Long ago, the spirits of the wind gave the island’s people magical instruments, devices, and animated constructs. Across generations, the Windshapers cared for these gifts. Then the spirits departed, and their patronage ended. Most creations fell into disrepair. Only a handful still work. One of Valanaar’s last working constructs has been damaged. Its loss would further diminish the island’s dwindling heritage. Artisan Riaani Nightwind was sent to the city’s western edge to examine the machine and try to repair it. These ancient devices are fragile, and she needs aid.

quest:93736.text: Unwelcome Spirits. The Windshapers seek the spirits of the wind, gone from their reach. Now hollows appear in Shadowgale Forest, and the order gathers their essences to learn what drove the true spirits away. The Windshapers have lost communion with the spirits of the wind. They seek to learn why the spirits left and what might bring them back. Their departure has left a void in the local elemental atmosphere. After the wind spirits departed, strange sprites called hollows appeared in Shadowgale Forest to the north. The Windshapers had not known of them before the spirits vanished. The hollows seem tied to the spirits’ absence, and their essences may help reveal what they are.

quest:93737.text: The Broken Construct. Ayessa has sent you to help Riaani Nightwind with a disabled construct. Hear his plans and learn what he needs done to set the machine right. Ayessa sends you to help Riaani Nightwind with a damaged construct. He is deep among its inner parts, searching for the cause of the trouble. Surprised by your arrival, Riaani doubts an untrained traveler can manage delicate mechanical work. Once he climbs out, he agrees to explain what needs doing. A construct depends on precise assembly and careful calibration. When it breaks down, its engineer faces serious work. Riaani Nightwind is shoulder-deep in mechanical parts and needs another pair of hands to gather materials or test the machine in the field. Listen to his briefing to learn how you can help bring the inert construct back to working order.

quest:93738.text: The Broken Construct. A Windshaper asks you to tell Ayessa Dawnsinger what you learned about the broken construct. The High Order’s work with wind spirit magic has drawn concern. Take what you learned to Ayessa Dawnsinger in Valanaar. The High Order has tested the Windshapers’ patience with its experiments in wind spirit magic. It has also touched knowledge under Windshaper purview. Ayessa can decide what should happen next.

quest:93739.text: Exploring the Horde. From Grommash Hold, you travel to meet the leaders who guide the Horde. The journey carries you from Orgrimmar to the Darkspear trolls, the tauren and the Forsaken. Nazgrel sends you from Grommash Hold into the wider Horde lands. The fortress stands at the heart of Orgrimmar, where Nazgrel and the Warchief's council oversee military affairs. You leave Durotar's red canyons behind to learn how far the peoples beneath the red banner are joined. You meet the leaders of the Horde's allied peoples: Shadow Hunter Vol'jin of the Darkspear trolls, High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof of the tauren, and Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, queen of the Forsaken. Speaking with each in person lets you see the ties between Kalimdor and Lordaeron, across the Great Sea, where plague has scarred the land.

quest:93740.text: Blood for Blood. Several Windshaper novices lie dead in the Highlands, and the Windshapers suspect the Al'Aketh. Ayessa sends you north to the Gustberry Lowlands to answer the killings and bring back the fallen cultists' windstone prayer charms. Several Windshaper novices have been found slain in the Highlands. Proof is scarce, yet the Windshapers suspect the Al'Aketh cultists. Their zealotry makes them the chief suspects. The Windshapers' creed demands an eye for an eye, so they will not let the killings go unanswered. Ayessa calls for you to strike at any Al'Aketh you find north in the Gustberry Lowlands. She asks you to bring back the windstone prayer charms carried by the fallen cultists, as proof of their deaths. The Windshapers see this strike as an answer to the cultists' long fanaticism.

quest:93746.text: A Firm Response. Ayessa Dawnsinger answers the High Order’s intrusion on Zephras Isle with force. She sends you after Belathaan Brightwish on the road north to the Shrine of Akir, to make the Windshapers’ boundaries clear. The Windshapers of Zephras Isle will not accept the High Order’s secretive scrutiny. Their warnings have gone unheeded, so Ayessa Dawnsinger escalates the dispute. She sends you to intercept Belathaan Brightwish on the lonely road north to the Shrine of Akir, away from prying eyes in town.

quest:93791.text: Speak with Belann. In Valanaar, aspiring spellcasters are sent to meet Belann Windwood. The High Order honors the making of a personal spell focus as a long-held tradition. As students grow in command of magic, the High Order turns to an ancient custom to test and strengthen their talents. Making a spell focus of their own, whether a wand or staff, is one of the order’s most enduring traditions. It is for students who wish to bind their growing power to an implement they have made themselves. In Valanaar, initiates seek Belann Windwood for help with this craft. He has spent more than a century forging staves and wands for the High Order. A trusted mentor, Belann welcomes dedicated students and guides them through the craft and history of their magical tools.

quest:93797.text: Boughs in the Wind. In Valanaar, Belann Windwood guides apprentices through the old rite of shaping a spell focus. They seek a wind-touched branch near Falaath Village, as fewer people in Zephras are born with a gift for magic. Young spellcasters in Zephras begin this old rite when they show a gift for magic. In Valanaar, Belann Windwood guides apprentices as they gather a fallen branch from the region’s oldest trees. The boughs keep traces of wind, making them fit to channel spells. The strongest boughs lie near the wind shrine just south of Falaath Village, where elemental currents gather. Tradition says a branch may choose its spellcaster, and some say it sings softly to those able to wield its power. For elders like Belann, each apprentice who completes the rite helps carry their culture forward. Fewer people in Zephras are born with a gift for magic each passing year.

quest:93835.text: Confront Lorthuna. An injured mage needs you to follow Ayessa Dawnsinger and Elaadrin Evengale through a portal to the Rohashi Spires. There, they face High Priestess Lorthuna and need your help. Lorthuna fled through a portal to the spires above. Ayessa Dawnsinger and Elaadrin Evengale followed moments ago, but their companion is too badly hurt to go with them. Join the two mages through the portal as they face the High Priestess.

quest:93926.text: The Western Watch. At the outpost southwest of the settlement, cultists press the defenders, and local leaders call them back. They judge the tower too costly to hold and turn to protecting the village. The western watchtower guards the frontier southwest of the settlement. Cultists have renewed their assault, and local leaders decide the isolated post costs too many lives to defend. So they prepare orders recalling the peacekeepers. They hope to spare more lives and gather every defender to protect the village and its people.

quest:93927.text: A Last Request. On Zephras, a fallen peacekeeper carries a message that may reveal his final moments. His bloodstained note points to the duty he left unfinished. You find a dead peacekeeper in the field with a bloodstained note in his hands. When you examine him, the note slips free. On Zephras, peacekeepers risk their lives to keep order. His last words may tell what happened to him. The bloodied parchment holds the peacekeeper's final plea or instructions. Whoever killed him left his duty unfinished. Read the clues and complete his final mission. The note points the way to answer his dying call.

quest:93948.text: Deliver the Signet. A traveler carries the recovered Shadowsong Family Signet to High Elder Talaanis Shadowsong in Valanaar. Its return confirms his nephew's death on Zephras Isle, and Talaanis points the traveler toward the local peacekeepers. A traveler carries the Shadowsong Family Signet to Valanaar, recovered from an isolated tower. The grim token is meant for Talaanis Shadowsong, the High Elder of Zephras Isle. His people love him, though hardship weighs on the settlement. The ring confirms his nephew has perished, and Talaanis receives the heirloom with condolences. In Valanaar, High Elder Talaanis thanks the traveler for returning the signet, though grief shadows him. He recognizes the traveler's skill and points them to Captain Valennia Stormfist, who leads the Valanaar peacekeepers. The settlement faces strained circumstances and mounting pressures. Its protectors welcome capable hands.

quest:93949.text: Bugged. In Valanaar, seasonal skyhopper swarms now threaten the settlement. High Order mages found listening enchantments on slain insects, and local cultists are suspected of spying through them. When skyhopper season comes, lowland insects swarm around Valanaar. High Order mages inspected several slain skyhoppers and found listening enchantments on them. Local cultists are suspected of using the seasonal pests to eavesdrop on the city. The enchanted skyhoppers look like ordinary insects, so Valanaar's protectors must cull the whole swarm. Clearing them out denies the hostile cult intelligence and ends its magical surveillance of the city.

quest:93951.text: A Little Beauty. In the Shen'dar Highlands, the Skyborne gather hippogryph down near Zephras. Its bright plumes bring beauty and small joys to the village through hard times. Wild hippogryphs nest on Zephras Isle, southwest of the village in the Shen'dar Highlands. They are territorial and can trouble travelers nearby. Yet they shed vibrant, silky soft down, which the Skyborne gather to weave into hair ornaments. For Zephras's artisan, gathering feathers for hair is more than vanity. Even in hard times, small joys shared with others help keep the community's spirit alive. Beauty gives each day in the village something to celebrate.

quest:93963.text: Exploring the Alliance. In Stormwind Keep, you begin a journey to meet the rulers of Ironforge and Darnassus. Their lands show you the breadth of the Alliance before you turn toward Westfall. Randal Emerson, an attendant in Stormwind Keep’s southern antechamber, sends you beyond the human capital. Newly arrived on Azeroth, you are invited to see the Alliance’s allied peoples firsthand. The journey takes you beyond the keep to learn the distinct cultures, traditions, and strength of those who stand with Stormwind. Your travels cross land and sea to the leaders of the Alliance. In Ironforge, you meet King Magni Bronzebeard in the mountain halls and High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, leader of the displaced gnomes. In Darnassus atop Teldrassil, you meet High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Their cities and peoples reveal the ties among humans, dwarves, gnomes, and night elves. After the long journey, you return to Stormwind. Knowing more of Azeroth helps you aid your own people, while your order prepares to establish itself in Dalaran. For now, the troubled territories near the capital need help, beginning with Westfall’s struggling farmlands.

quest:94003.text: The Skybreaker Bulwark. At the Shrine of Akir, Zaal Stormshield holds the Skybreaker Bulwark. The last of the Skybreakers seeks its return from the cultist who took it. On Zephras Isle, the Al'Aketh have slain the Skybreakers, leaving one survivor. The last of the family bears deep sorrow and bitter shame over the loss of their greatest heirloom. The cultist Zaal Stormshield took the Skybreaker Bulwark and now lurks at the Shrine of Akir. By family tradition, the Skybreaker Bulwark protects anyone truly worthy to wield it. The last Skybreaker believes Zaal unworthy of its divine favor. So the survivor seeks an adventurer to strike down the thief at the Shrine of Akir and reclaim the ancestral shield. In return, the Skybreaker offers training in the Skybreaker Defense technique.

quest:94007.text: Taming the Beast. In Valanaar, Quel'ana Quickgale can teach you to tame a beast. Your time in the highlands has prepared you to seek an animal companion. Your host believes you are ready to seek an animal companion after your time in the highlands. Go to Valanaar and speak with Quel'ana Quickgale. He will teach you the art of beast taming.

quest:94013.text: Taming the Beast. Quel'ana Quickgale gives you one last trial in taming a Vuldren Alpha. Mastering it prepares you for the deeper teachings of your class. Quel'ana gives you a Taming Rod and sends you to the Gustberry Lowlands. There, you are to tame a Vuldren Alpha. Then return the rod to him in Valanaar. This trial proves your mastery and prepares you for deeper class teachings.

quest:94050.text: Training the Beast. In Valanaar, you meet Quel'dora Quickgale to learn how to train your pet. Her teaching helps you care for and guide it. Your fellow hunter sends you to his sister, Quel'dora Quickgale, in Valanaar. You already know how to tame a pet. Now Quel'dora can teach you to train your companion. Quel'dora teaches you to guide your pet, teach it new abilities, feed it, and revive it if it falls in battle. She urges you to respect the balance and remain in awe of the nature around you.

quest:94222.text: Craftsman's Writ: Iridescent Hammer. A customer awaits one Iridescent Hammer, with delivery and payment details set down in a writ. Its transferable mark lets the holder complete the exchange. The customer asks for one Iridescent Hammer. Bring the writ to complete the exchange at the marked location.

quest:94243.text: Craftsman's Writ: Heavy Quiver. A faded Craftsman's Writ: Heavy Quiver asks you to bring one Heavy Quiver to a marked location and gives payment details. The note asks you to acquire one Heavy Quiver and bring it to the place marked on your map. Keep the writ with you to complete the exchange.

quest:94253.text: Craftsman's Writ: Colorful Kilt. A customer seeks a disguise for slipping into Zul'Gurub, and Craftsman's Writ: Colorful Kilt names the garment they want. The transferable writ asks you to bring one Colorful Kilt to the marked location. The customer plans to pass through Zul'Gurub's gates dressed as one of its ritualists, and says the kilt suits the disguise.

quest:94369.text: The Fate of Zephras. In Valanaar, you bring Talaanis Shadowsong word of the danger facing Zephras. The fallen wards leave the isle exposed to Al'Akir, and its people must decide how to protect their home. You tell Talaanis what happened above the Shrine of Akir. You share Elaadrin's plan to leave Zephras Isle. High Elder Shadowsong needs to understand the danger and why you were sent to Azeroth. The people of Zephras must find a way to save their home.

quest:94373.text: Call of Earth. At Anvilmar, Teo Hammerstorm tests initiates who seek the earth's favor. They face Frostmane trolls to the south and claim bear pendants before receiving an earthen sapta. In Coldridge Valley, Teo Hammerstorm guides initiates at Anvilmar along the earth's rugged path. He teaches young wanderers to heed the mountains and see the land as firm ground. Stone can shield those who respect it. The earth shares its wisdom only with those who show grit and patience. To prove they are ready, initiates face Frostmane trolls in a cave south of Anvilmar. The trolls make coarse pendants from Iceclaw bears that roam the frozen heights. Recovering two bear pendants from the den proves the stubborn resolve and strength the elemental spirits expect.

quest:94374.text: Call of Earth. At a mountain Spirit Stone, an initiate drinks Earth Sapta and binds spirit to the world's enduring foundations. The draught opens the way to elemental awareness, teaching humility and patience amid snow and rock. At an isolated mountain shrine, you drink Earth Sapta, an enchanted brew. Ancient elemental magic gives it power to show mortal eyes elemental spirits and subtle currents beyond ordinary sight. Its strength makes the shrine the only safe place to drink it, where spirit and stone can form their bond. High on a snow-swept mountain, the Spirit Stone waits at the end of a secluded path. You travel through bitter cold to stand humbly before the ancient rock. The living earth welcomes those who come without pride. Mountains give lasting physical strength, while the vast, steady plains teach patience. Communion with stone is a foundational rite for spiritual pathfinders. Wind, fire, and crashing water carry restless fury, while earth teaches discipline and quiet resilience. You absorb earth's still essence, preparing mind and body for the conflicting, chaotic dualities of the more volatile elements that roar across the world.

quest:94375.text: Call of Earth. Young shaman in Dun Morogh seek the earth spirits’ favor through Call of Earth. They carry rough quartz to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar, where he shapes it into the heart of an Earth Totem. In Dun Morogh, young shaman begin their spiritual path by seeking the earth spirit and listening to its teachings. The spirit gives them rough quartz, a humble stone meant to become the heart of an Earth Totem. The rite calls for humility, patience, strength, and resolve. An initiate learns from the earth and does not measure worth by size. Teo Hammerstorm waits in Anvilmar for the initiate to bring back the rough quartz. He judges whether the mountain spirits have acknowledged them, and sends away anyone who arrives without the stone. Bring him the quartz, and he shapes it into an Earth Totem. The totem binds the young shaman to the strength of the world's roots.

quest:94411.text: Meddlesome Mages. In the Shen'dar Highlands, High Order apprentices gather at sacred stones and meddle with magic. Their spells threaten the fragile forces that hold the island together. North of the village, High Order apprentices gather around ancient standing stones. Repeated warnings have not turned them from the sacred sites. They press on with their arcane studies, while local leaders hesitate to shed the blood of their shen'dorei kin. So they call for outside help to drive the apprentices away before lasting harm is done. Delicate mystical forces bind the island's land together and keep it safe. The defenders fear the High Order gives little thought to the danger in its spellcraft. One careless spell could break those bindings. Then ruin would come to everyone who lives there.

quest:94413.text:
A Magical Affront. On Zephras, A Magical Affront sets the local order against the Windshapers. The order seeks to harness and study the surfaced leylines, while the Windshapers see them as scars to heal. Their conflict has reached the southwestern forest. Ancient conduits of raw magic have recently broken through the earth on Zephras. For scholars and practitioners of the local order, this is a rare boon. Direct contact with the leylines gives them new insight into the arcane currents across the region and deepens their mastery of magic. The Windshapers see the exposed energies as open wounds and scars across Zephras. They gather at the rupture sites to suppress or mend the leylines and heal the earth.

The order depends on that raw power, so it sees their efforts as a threat. It sends you southwest into the forest to drive the Windshapers back.

quest:94414.text: The Anchors of Zephras. On Zephras Isle, Halaan Hawk-Eye asks you to watch the ancient anchor pylons that hold the island aloft. Their magic has begun to waver, and the wind spirits' blessing may no longer be steady. Wind spirits gave Zephras's ancient anchor pylons the power to bind and sustain the floating island. Their magic keeps the land steady amid the churning skies. From afar, the towering monoliths look untouched. Yet the island depends on the wind spirits' continuing blessing. The anchor pylons look proud and undamaged, yet their magic has grown erratic. Halaan Hawk-Eye says the harmony that sustains them has become unstable and uncertain. No clear sign of physical harm appears. Those who watch over the groves have reason to fear what threatens the isle. Halaan Hawk-Eye cannot use skysight to peer between worlds, nor can he tap Zephras's deep ley lines. His gift is natural vision sharp enough to reach immense distances. He lends that sight to newcomers, so they can study the distant pylons and watch for changes in their homeland's fate.

quest:94427.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Your order sends you to Tanis Alderwood in Undercity’s Trade Quarter. There, a chance to show grace comes through good deeds. Your order teaches that divinity means doing good for its own sake, not seeking godhood. It says tragedy brought you here. Now it asks you to find Tanis Alderwood in Undercity’s Trade Quarter. Tanis is in need and may benefit from your grace.

quest:94434.text: A Lesson in Divinity. In the Undercity, Tanis Alderwood asks you for fresh cloth. His wife is falling apart, and he hopes to wrap her until an apothecary is free. The apothecaries are occupied with the Dark Lady's business. So Tanis asks you to bring linen for his wife. He hopes the cloth will hold her together while they wait for help.

quest:94435.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Tanis Alderwood thanks you for your help and calls you a friend. Danitha Morr sees this small act of service as a way to strengthen the Forsaken’s connection to the Light. Danitha Morr says your help may strengthen the Forsaken’s connection to the Light. Mistrust and conspiracies linger among the Dark Lady’s followers. The Forsaken must meet that fear with courage and righteousness. Danitha gives you a symbol for what comes next.

quest:94436.text: A Lesson in Divinity. In A Lesson in Divinity, Danitha Morr asks you to show what a priest can do with the Symbol of Life. Deathguard Billmuth at Bandarion Keep has come seeking aid for a friend. Billmuth says the priests turned him away, and his friend may have no one else to turn to. He is not proud to ask you, but he needs aid for the Forsaken. The Symbol of Life is meant to show your ability to channel the Light. Handling it may cause discomfort. Its power can still be your ally and guide, even to the Forsaken, whose creation is tied to a force opposed to the Light.

quest:94438.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Danitha Morr sends you to Venomweb Vale to find Deathguard Falgan. He and his companion were separated after learning the Scarlet Crusade plans an attack on Brill. Deathguard Falgan went with Billmuth to scout Scarlet activity in Venomweb Vale. They learned the Scarlet Crusade plans some kind of attack. Now Falgan asks whether you will help the Forsaken further.

quest:94440.text: A Lesson in Divinity. Deathguard Billmuth needs you to recover Scarlet Crusade attack plans from Venomweb Vale. The Deathguard expects an assault and hopes the plans will help prepare an ambush. Scarlet Crusaders carry deployment orders in their satchels, and the Deathguard expects an attack. Bring a copy of the plans to Deathguard Billmuth at Bandarion Keep. Then the Deathguard can prepare an ambush.

quest:94441.text: A Lesson in Divinity. A fellow Forsaken asks you to thank Danitha Morr for the paladins’ service at Bandarion Keep. Your work has earned the Deathguard’s gratitude and brings a gift of redemption. A fellow Forsaken asks you to carry their thanks to Danitha Morr at Bandarion Keep. The rest of the Deathguard will hear of the service you and the other paladins performed. They are proud to count you among the Forsaken and trust the Dark Lady watches over you.

quest:94449.text: Call of Fire. In Dun Morogh, an elder sends shaman initiates to Bruegs Kindleborn to test their readiness for the fire sapta. They have already learned patience and grounding through earth. After proving patience and grounding through earth, shamans face a more volatile force: the fire elemental spirit. Stone holds steady, but fire promises chaos, ruin, and fierce energy. So an elder sends the initiate across Dun Morogh’s snow-laden peaks to seek guidance before trying to harness its wild heat. Bruegs Kindleborn keeps watch in a secluded cave high in the mountains above South Gate Outpost. When an initiate arrives with an elder’s recommendation, Bruegs prepares them for the sapta of fire. He warns that flame’s hunger to burn and consume is easily stirred. To master it, a shaman must know when to hold back.

quest:94493.text: A Sacrifice in Vain. Elegael Thornpaw fears the Al'Aketh Cultists will overwhelm the wounded in her den. A message meant for Valanaar has not reached them, leaving her to ask for help. The Al'Aketh Cultists fell upon Elegael Thornpaw's fellows with almost no warning. Many in her den are wounded or dying, and she does not know how long they can survive the attack. She had tried to send word to Valanaar, but the message did not get through. With no reinforcements in sight, Elegael asks you to help.

quest:94792.text: Taming the Beast. Josephine Carson is teaching aspiring hunters in Taming the Beast how to care for a wild companion. The trial uses a Rockhide Boar and a Taming Rod, with nature’s balance in mind. Traveling alone in the wild can be dangerous. An animal companion offers protection in battle and company on long journeys. For aspiring hunters and trackers, forming that bond is a vital step. Josephine Carson guides novices through a trial with a Rockhide Boar and a Taming Rod. To calm and direct the beast, they must stay composed and focused without giving in to fear or causing needless bloodshed. Josephine Carson warns her pupils not to exploit beasts recklessly. Taming calls for patience and discipline, never cruelty or dominance, and nature’s balance must be kept. The enchanted rod lets novices practice handling a formidable Rockhide Boar without permanently depleting local wildlife. Once they learn to command and soothe the beast, they return the rod. Respect for nature comes before pride.

quest:94793.text: Training the Beast. In Goldshire, Training the Beast shows young hunters how to care for a tamed companion. Isaac Chan teaches them to feed and revive their beasts, then train them for life at their side. You seek Isaac Chan, an experienced woodsman in Goldshire, to learn how to train your beast. A tamed creature needs care and discipline before it can become a steady ally. Without Chan's guidance, your companion may remain unruly in the wilderness. Isaac Chan teaches you to care for your animal companion. You learn to feed it and revive it if it falls in battle. He also teaches commands that help it fight, and reminds you that power over wildlife calls for respect. Honor nature's balance and live in awe of the world around you.

quest:94863.text: Taming the Beast. Josephine Carson guides you through Taming the Beast as you learn to handle a boar before facing a Gray Forest Wolf. With a Taming Rod, you seek the fiercer creature's trust. Josephine Carson watches as you take another step in learning to handle beasts. You have practiced with simple boars; now you enter the forest to tame a Gray Forest Wolf. The enchanted rod she gives you helps calm the predator. Patience and respect matter as much as tracking and marksmanship when you seek a wild creature's trust. Josephine Carson gives you a specialized Taming Rod to calm dangerous wildlife. Approach the wolf with patience and precision, and overcome its aggression without lethal force. After practicing your bond with the beast, return the rod to Josephine as proof of your growing skill.

quest:94864.text: Taming the Beast. In Elwynn Forest, hunters face Taming the Beast, the final trial Josephine Carson oversees. After taming a boar and a wolf, each hunter uses a Taming Rod to earn a Young Forest Bear’s trust. The test deepens the hunter’s bond with beasts and teaches respect for the woodland’s balance. Hunters in Elwynn Forest learn to live among the wild creatures around them. After taming a wolf and a boar, they face one last test of courage and patience. Josephine Carson sends each hunter to a Young Forest Bear, the strongest of the forest’s common predators. The hunter must endure the bear’s strength and earn its trust, rather than force it to submit. Taming wildlife in Elwynn calls for respect, not dominion. Forest bears embody the woodland’s strength and vitality, and help keep its natural order. With a Taming Rod, hunters learn to calm a bear’s aggression and form a bond through understanding. Earning the trust of such a powerful animal deepens a hunter’s bond with the wild and completes the first lessons Josephine Carson oversees.

quest:94911.text: Child of Nature. A fellow Skyborne sees promise in your druidic arts and points you toward Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff. He can teach you how to reach the Cenarion Circle’s stronghold in Moonglade. Your teacher believes the druids of the Cenarion Circle will welcome you and share their knowledge. Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff can show you how to reach their stronghold in Moonglade.

quest:94912.text: Child of Nature. In Stormwind, Sheldras Moontree can show you the way to Moonglade. There, the Cenarion Circle’s druids have wisdom to share with a child of nature. Sheldras Moontree, a night elf in Stormwind, can show you how to reach Moonglade on Kalimdor. The Cenarion Circle keeps its stronghold there. It is an ancient order of naturalists and druids, with much to teach you.

quest:94914.text: Moonglade. Your teacher opens a way to Moonglade, where Dendrite Starblaze awaits. There, you can speak with him about the path you have begun. Your teacher welcomes druids to Moonglade. Keeper Remulos watches over those who rest there. You receive Teleport: Moonglade, a spell that carries you there when you seek knowledge or solace. Your first lesson is to speak with Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven about the path you now follow.

quest:94946.text:
The Magical City of Dalaran. A mage in Valanaar sends you from Zephras Isle to Dalaran City, where several mages await your people's arrival. The city offers a place to begin exploring Azeroth, but the lands beyond can be dangerous without preparation and experience. Recent events with the cult keep the speaker in Valanaar for now. Several mages wait in Dalaran for your people, so you are sent to the dock outside the lodge. There, you board a skycutter bound for Dalaran City.

When you arrive, speak with Danaaris Stargale. Your people are still making their home in the city, and the country beyond its safety can prove dangerous.

quest:94978.text: Taming the Beast. Quel'ana Quickgale teaches you the bond between beast and master. You begin by taming a Windsong Crawler near the waters of Zephras. You have the Taming Rod and a Windsong Crawler to tame. Find one near a body of water and practice your skills. Then return the rod to Quel'ana Quickgale in Valanaar. This creature is your first step toward mastery.

quest:94979.text: Taming the Beast. In the Gustberry Lowlands, Quel'ana Quickgale asks you to tame a galestrider. Your skill on open ground will prepare you for trials ahead. You've already shown you can tame the river's crawler. Now Quel'ana Quickgale gives you a Taming Rod and sends you to the lowlands of Zephras. There, a proud, winged galestrider runs swiftly across the plains. Earn its trust and practice your skill. Then bring the rod back to Quel'ana in Valanaar.

quest:95041.text: Data Hoarders. Outside Gnomeregan, Jemma Quikswitch searches the snow for lost punch cards. The exiled gnome lives in Ironforge, and the cards hold her family's archives, from submarine designs to family recipes. Without them, the records she still has remain unreadable. When troggs invaded Gnomeregan and radiation struck, thousands of gnomes fled with what they could carry. A damaged satchel spilled several of Jemma's cards into the snow around the fallen city. Without them, her surviving records read as gibberish, and her family's knowledge risks being lost. The Quikswitch archives hold arcanotechnical field equations and submarine hull blueprints from the Second War. They also preserve Grandma Quikswitch's secret chili recipe. For refugees in Ironforge, the comforts of home matter as much as engineering marvels.

quest:95042.text: Seeking the Kor Gem. In Ashenvale, Ulric Frostveil sees your search for a Kor Gem as familiar work for Alliance spellcasters. He points you north to Blackfathom Deeps, where naga still use the gems. Ulric asks you to bring him a Kor Gem from the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, north of Ashenvale. The naga below still use the gems. They can empower magical weapons and implements, but Ulric warns you not to go alone.

quest:95111.text: An Underrated Talent. In Silverpine Forest, Trevan Rol gives Ott a chance to make a blade to your design. Ott’s simple weapons have earned praise from smiths in the Undercity. Trevan Rol asks you to carry materials to Ott in Tarren Mill and offer him a commission. Ott sells simple blades to travelers. Trevan bought one and later took it to the Undercity for maintenance. There, local smiths praised its quality and mistook it for the work of a famous master. Now Ott has the chance to forge a blade to your specifications.

quest:95125.text: Ott's Masterwork. Ott is ready to forge a blade for you from fine materials. You may watch him at work. Ott values the fine materials and hopes his work will meet your expectations. He forges a blade for you, then offers it for your travels.

quest:95126.text: The Moonsilver Blade. In Silverpine Forest, Trevan Rol awaits the blade that will complete his work before he faces a beast. Ott thanks you for the chance to help and asks you to carry his gratitude to Trevan. You bring Ott's Masterwork back to Trevan Rol in Silverpine Forest.

quest:95140.text: Old Fire-Eye. Lumina Windsinger sends you after Old Fire-Eye in Silverpine Forest with the Moonsilver Blade. The Windshapers await his death, and Lumina hopes the blade will guide you well. The Windshapers have given you the Moonsilver Blade. Locals say Old Fire-Eye hunts across a wide stretch south of here, usually near the gates to Gilneas. Lumina asks you to find him and use the blade to end him. The Windshapers' gratitude depends on his death.

quest:95212.text: Never Saddle on Quality. At Amberstill Ranch, handlers prepare rams for the Alliance expedition in Alterac. They need pristine mountain leopard pelts to make warm saddles for the beasts, so mounts and riders can face the northern mountains' biting frost. The handlers of Amberstill Ranch in Dun Morogh are readying sturdy mountain rams for Alterac. But the work has stalled: they lack the material needed to make durable, cold-weather saddles for the rams. The expedition's mounts need thick insulation to endure the freeze of the Alterac mountains. Hunters are sent to the eastern crags to track the largest, fiercest mountain leopards in Dun Morogh and bring back pristine pelts. The Alliance forces need gear that can withstand the high passes.

quest:95213.text: Stolen Blasting Powder. Near Gol'Bolar Quarry, an empty keg of hazardous blasting powder has turned up among troggs. Its return to Quarrymaster Thesten reveals a breach in the quarry's security and explosive stores. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, a warning stamped on an empty keg shows that hazardous blasting powder has slipped out of authorized hands. The explosives are reserved for controlled quarrying, with the quarrymaster's direct approval. The keg was found among hostile troggs, and that points to a threat beyond ordinary trouble for the miners.

quest:95214.text: Stolen Blasting Powder. At Gol'Bolar Quarry, Stolen Blasting Powder has gone east with the troggs. Quarrymaster Thesten needs help recovering the missing munitions before the brutes set them off by accident. At Gol'Bolar Quarry in Dun Morogh, dwarves use heavy blasting charges to break stone and open deep veins. But primitive troggs from the nearby crags stole a bulk shipment of high-grade powder. Quarrymaster Thesten needs capable hands before the pack causes an accidental detonation. The missing keg holds enough force to reduce King Magni Bronzebeard's grand throne room to an open-air courtyard. The troggs carried the powder east to their rough foothill camps. Left alone, they may soon discover fire or strike stone against spark.

quest:95217.text:
The Quarry's Smith. At the quarry, The Quarry's Smith, Frast Dokner, needs metal and leather for camp repairs. With a supply shipment late, he asks travelers to bring the materials. In return, Dokner offers practical smithing techniques. An excavation needs steady care. Pickaxes must be sharpened, worn brackets replaced, and camp gear reinforced. When a vital shipment misses its schedule, work begins to grind to a halt. Without fresh stock from the major trade routes, the craftsmen must improvise and look to passing travelers for help.

Frast Dokner works the forge through these delays. He asks anyone willing to gather basic metals and hides to help keep the camp running, rather than wait for transport wagons that may be far behind. Dwarven blacksmithing guilds prize discipline and guard their methods, rarely sharing trade secrets with casual wanderers. Dokner weighs that custom against the camp's immediate needs. He lacks workable copper and durable leather for patching tools and camp gear.

Bring the raw materials to his anvil, and he will teach you his personal smithing techniques. The bargain trades useful craft knowledge for materials the camp needs to endure and keep its gear in repair.

quest:95314.text:
That Shadowvale Green Elixir. In Brill, That Shadowvale Green Elixir draws buyers despite the old ban. Shadowvale's secluded villagers once brewed Whispering Elixir from local herbs, and the Scourge left the village in ruins. Before the Scourge came, Shadowvale's villagers brewed Whispering Elixir from rare herbs found only in Tirisfal Glades. The draught grew known across northern Lordaeron. The Capital City outlawed it, yet mystics, poisoners, and apothecaries still sought its unusual properties, defying royal decrees. Shadowvale lies deep in the Whispering Forest of western Tirisfal. Its people were insular and distrustful, and rarely welcomed outsiders. The Scourge invasion left the settlement in ruins, though forgotten stores of aged green elixir remain among the wreckage.

Carolai Anise works from Brill. The underworld still wants the brew, so she pays adventurers willing to brave the forest's unsettling silence.

quest:95328.text: Whispering Horror Residue. Beneath the Whispering Forest, Whispering Horror Residue is carried to Undercity for study. Father Lankester awaits it in the War Quarter. Beneath the Whispering Forest, you recover a strange beast’s twitching remains. The unsettling material is carried to Undercity, where researchers may study it. In Undercity’s War Quarter, Father Lankester receives the remains. He says the Whispering Forest has long been touched by the void. Its physical traces may help him study the mysteries of shadow.

quest:95507.text: Vrang's Game. Vrang sends you across a valley in the Barrens to check his traps. The small game they catch can help him, though other wildlife makes the area dangerous. Vrang has traps scattered across the valley, and he wants you to bring back any small game they have caught. Keep your attention on the wildlife too, for it can make the area dangerous.

quest:95508.text: Unwelcome Guests. You helped someone survive an encounter with unwelcome guests, and they are grateful. What brought you together remains unclear.

quest:95646.text: Horrors in the Highland. Rethiel the Greenwarden senses corruption flowing through a mountain gully into the Wetlands' freshwater. He sends you to the highland excavation sites for a Highland Horror's root core, then warns that digging stirs an ancient energy and endangers the whole region. Rethiel the Greenwarden senses the land changing deep in the Wetlands. Through a mountain gully, foul taint reaches the highlands and infects their freshwater creatures. Lowland life has been shaped by brackish water, but these creatures have never known the sea's protective salt. Rethiel fears they cannot withstand the spreading evil. He asks you to climb to the excavation sites, slay a Highland Horror, and bring back its root core.

quest:95647.text: Lost in the Thicket Things. Ardin Grassman is missing near an excavation site after following word of towering grasses. His alchemist wife asks travelers to find him, as dangerous wildlife has attacked the crew. Ardin Grassman's alchemist wife asks you to find her missing husband. He has a keen sense for nature and often braves cliffs and distant wilds to gather herbs and plants for her work. When an excavation crew spoke of towering grasses unlike any they had seen, Ardin's curiosity drew him toward the site.

quest:95737.text:
Seeking Caitlin. An alchemist waits for word about a rare grass. She asks you to find Caitlin Grassman in Menethil Harbor, whose husband has not reported back from an excavation. The alchemist heard from Caitlin that her husband's excavation team found signs of a primordial grass. Caitlin does not know how much they found or whether it can be reached.

Now the alchemist asks you to speak with Caitlin in Menethil Harbor. Both women are waiting to learn what happened to the promised seeds.

quest:95772.text: Songblade Search. Dorin Songblade waits for word from his brother Daewyn in the Wetlands. Daewyn joined an archaeological crew from Loch Modan to dig in unexplored hills, but his silence is unlike him. Dorin Songblade tends his workshop, buried in orders to refit girdles. His brother Daewyn has gone north with a dwarven excavation crew from Loch Modan. The hills they seek in the Wetlands have never felt a dwarven pickaxe. Daewyn usually writes as soon as he arrives, but no word has reached Dorin, and the silence unsettles him.

quest:95774.text: Her Name Is Olgra. Mankrik mourns Olgra and prepares a monument to keep her name alive. He asks you to seek her missing bone adornments among the nearby Razormane raiders. A healer saved Mankrik, but Olgra died from her wounds on the battlefield. Grieving, Mankrik prepares a lasting tribute so her name and sacrifice will be remembered. Olgra wore cherished ornaments made of polished bone, but they are missing from her resting place. Mankrik asks you to recover them from the nearby Razormane raiders, so they can rest beside the monument he is raising for her.

quest:95803.text: A Token of Good Faith. Danitha sends you to carry Rudolph Gelhardt’s head to Sylvanas Windrunner in the Undercity. The delivery is meant to show the Forsaken that your people are devoted to their prosperity. Danitha says Sylvanas distrusts your people and openly disparages them. She asks you to bring Rudolph Gelhardt’s head as proof that you tend to your own house and stand with the Forsaken.

quest:95805.text: Grace of An'she and Mu'sha. On Red Cloud Mesa, An'she and Mu'sha receive honor as the Earthmother's eyes. You carry smoldering incense to a shrine in the southeastern hills, where its smoke rises toward the sun and moon that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains. Tauren honor An'she and Mu'sha as the sun and moon, the Earthmother's twin eyes. Elemental spirits dwell in Azeroth's stones, winds, and waters, while the celestial twins watch from the heights of heaven. As they cross the sky, they mark day and night and bring warmth, guidance, and hope to living creatures. For tauren, honoring them is a spiritual duty. Balance calls for reverence toward the land beneath your feet and the light above. Carry smoldering incense into the southeastern hills overlooking Red Cloud Mesa, just south of the prickly quilboar grounds. Make the journey with speed and care. Keep the embers dry and reach the shrine before they burn to cold ash. At the elevated shrine, cast them into the sacred fire. Their fragrant smoke carries your respect skyward, toward the sun and moon.

quest:95998.text: The Great Outdoors. At Sam’s fire, travelers learn to rest and endure the road. Then they can turn to tradeskills and work in the wild. Sam welcomes restless travelers who cross Azeroth in search of fortune, danger, and renown. Ambition alone cannot keep a newcomer warm or ease the miles. By his fire, you learn when to rest, how to build a fire, and how to gather strength for the open road. A campfire offers warmth against the night chill and a chance for boosted rest. Those who know the wild understand that endurance comes from resting between journeys. Once you have learned these basics, you can turn to tradeskills. Craftsmen and gatherers can learn to make camp fixtures suited to their work in the field.

quest:960.text:
Onu is meditating. At the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, Onu enters a deep trance as a threat grows. The ancient of lore weighs the alliance and motives of the Twilight's Hammer cult and the naga. If you lose your scrying phial, speak to him for another. In the Grove of the Ancients, Onu holds Kalimdor's history in his ancient memory. Ominous reports of dark excavations at the Master's Glaive draw his vast consciousness inward. He considers what brings the fanatical Twilight's Hammer cultists and the naga to the petrified remains of an ancient behemoth. As you carry out his reconnaissance, Onu remains within reach and can replace a scrying phial misplaced in the wild. Onu uses nature-attuned divination to watch the ruins without risking his physical presence. He entrusts you with a scrying phial, which conjures a scrying bowl at the excavation site and lets him commune from afar. The journey south through Darkshore is perilous, with hostile wildlife and cultist patrols, so mishaps can happen.

Onu's trance is an attentive vigil, not unbroken slumber. He readily offers another vial of sacred waters so you can continue the investigation of the Master's Glaive.

quest:96031.text: Camping 101: Leatherworking. At a camp in the wilderness, leatherworkers put cured hides to use and make shelter of their own. A sound campsite needs a pitched tent and a fire, whose kindling is taught by cooking trainers. For tradespeople who work with hides and leather, making a shelter of their own is an essential milestone. A sturdy leather tent shields travelers from harsh weather, wind and the chill of night on open ground. Townsfolk frown on tents pitched in crowded streets or market squares, so you need to pass beyond the city gates and into the wilderness to make camp. A pitched tent is only half a campsite. A proper fire keeps back darkness and cold winds, and gives you a hearth in dangerous lands. Since cooking in the field begins with building and tending a fire, seek instruction from culinary masters and cooking trainers. They teach you to kindle a campfire before you establish camp.

quest:96044.text: Camping 101: Blacksmithing. Smiths bound for the wilderness are sent to Kharanos to learn from Tognus Flintfire. He teaches them to make a portable sharpening wheel for keeping weapons keen at camp. You are sent to Kharanos to learn how a smith can serve far from a town forge. There, skilled hands turn raw metal into tools for camp. A blade kept keen is ready for the long road. In Kharanos, Tognus Flintfire teaches capable smiths to make a sharpening wheel. Set one beside your campsite and warriors and rogues can grind nicks from their weapons and hone dull edges before the next march.

quest:96045.text: Camping 101: Alchemy. In Ironforge, Vosur Brakthel shows alchemists how to prepare for the road. With a Mana Well, they can give spellcasters and healers a place to recover while traveling. Vosur Brakthel trains alchemists in Ironforge to carry their craft beyond the city. Brewing vials in a quiet laboratory is only part of the work. Out in Azeroth's wild places, alchemists can use what they know to make a Mana Well for a camp, helping companions endure the journey. A Mana Well can refresh healers and spellcasters, but it belongs at a wilderness camp, not on an Ironforge street. City folk frown on tents pitched within their walls. A proper camp also needs a fire, so seek a cooking trainer's guidance before heading into the wild.

quest:96046.text: Camping 101: Mining. Out beyond the guarded roads, miners learn to make a lodestone for a wilderness camp. The work pairs knowledge of stone with the firecraft needed to live outdoors. Beyond guarded roads, a miner must rely on fieldcraft. Mineral knowledge gives you the means to shape a lodestone, the anchor for a campsite in the wild. A campsite belongs beyond town limits, where travelers can pitch their shelters without troubling settled folk. Choose a place in the open wilds. A camp also needs a fire to ward off the night chill. Learning to build one is part of the same fieldcraft as working stone.

quest:96047.text: Camping 101: First Aid. In Kharanos, Thamner Pol teaches you to prepare First Aid Kits for camps in Dun Morogh. With these supplies, travelers can stay alive in the field. You can build on your basic bandaging skills by learning to prepare supplies for a resting site. Thamner Pol shows you how raw medical supplies become complete kits, ready for use at camp when travelers need care far from shelter. Thamner Pol teaches you practical ways to outfit expedition sites with emergency supplies. A proper field kit lets a group bind wounds and regain strength together by the hearth before heading back into the cold.

quest:96050.text: Camping 101: Fishing. You’re preparing for wilderness fishing with a Fish Bowl and a campfire. Learn where to set up and what makes a resting place comfortable. Travel through Azeroth calls for a little knowledge of the wild. When you need a place to rest, keep your tent and gear beyond town borders. Townsfolk and guards dislike travelers spreading their belongings through settlements. Take your supplies into the open wilderness instead. A proper campsite needs a few comforts. Start with a warm campfire; a cooking trainer can teach you how to make one. Once the fire is ready, set out a handcrafted Fish Bowl. Then your stop is fit for an angler.

quest:96055.text: Camping 101: Herbalism. In Ironforge, herbalists can learn to make Incense Candles for life in camp. Reyna Stonebranch teaches the craft to gatherers ready to put wild herbs to practical use. Gathering wild herbs can serve a camp as well as a traveling party. With skill, herbalists turn what they gather into useful aids for life outdoors. In Ironforge, proficient herbalists can seek instruction from Reyna Stonebranch. Once they prove their skill, she teaches them to make an Incense Candle. Its soothing aroma lifts the spirits at camp and brings calm to spellcasters and healers on long expeditions.

quest:96056.text: Camping 101: Skinning. In Ironforge, skilled skinners learn to make a Camp Chair from animal hides. Balthus Stoneflayer teaches the craft after they prove their skill. Skinning fallen beasts gives armorers and crafters leather to work with. Hides from cats, bears, and other beasts have uses in the field, too. You are sent to turn those materials into something useful at camp instead of selling them. Balthus Stoneflayer teaches skinners in Ironforge to make a Camp Chair from prepared pelts. First, you need to show him you know how to skin beasts. Only then will he share his crafting methods. A Camp Chair gives you a place to sit by the fire and unwind while traveling. Rest there, and you can meet the next danger with your senses sharp and your strength restored.

quest:96101.text:
The Great Outdoors. Raan welcomes new wanderers and shows them how to endure the wild. Rest by his basic campfire to gain Boosted Rest, then visit nearby trade trainers to learn practical professions. Raan has traveled the wilds and teaches others how to survive beyond settlement walls. Ambition and steel alone will not carry you through harsh weather; practical campcraft matters. He welcomes those seeking fortune and glory, and offers guidance to anyone willing to learn. Raan asks you to sit beside his basic campfire and rest until you gain Boosted Rest. Across Azeroth's wild places, knowing when to pause, make camp, and recover can mean the difference between life and death.

After the lesson, Raan directs you to nearby village trainers. There you can learn a trade and craft specialized fixtures for your campsite.

quest:96102.text: Camping 101: Tailoring. Tailoring training teaches you to make a Rallying Banner. Its test belongs in the wilderness, where a camp needs a campfire. You can now craft a Rallying Banner, and its completion note calls for a wilderness test. A camp needs a campfire before you set it up. Most cooks can teach you to make one, so ask a cooking trainer for the basics if you have not learned them.

quest:96130.text: Chakuyak. Near the tree stands west of Stonebull Lake, Chakuyak threatens travelers crossing Mulgore. Local tribesfolk have marked the fierce wolf for hunting, and her pelt will be honored. Chakuyak prowls the tree stands west of Stonebull Lake, where prairie wolves roam Mulgore’s grassy plateaus and rolling hills. This fierce alpha female has become a danger to travelers arriving from abroad, so local hunters have marked her for removal before more wanderers are harmed. For the local tribes, killing Chakuyak calls for solemn respect, not boasting. They see it as necessary to protect travelers and villagers. Her thick pelt is cured and put to use, honoring the wolf and ensuring her sacrifice is not wasted.

quest:96243.text: Call of Earth. In Coldridge Valley, the Call of Earth sends an initiate to seek Teo Hammerstorm at Anvilmar. There begins a shaman’s communion with the spirits of stone. An initiate’s first communion with the elements begins when the earth calls. Other elemental energies may already stir, but speaking with stone brings balance. The earth teaches the initiate to find strength that will not yield. Firm footing comes beneath their boots and within their spirit. In Dun Morogh’s snowy reaches, initiates find shelter and instruction at Anvilmar. The holdfast lies in Coldridge Valley, forged by hammer, fire, and will. Teo Hammerstorm waits within, teaching fledgling shamans to heed the rumbling earth and begin their elemental duties.

quest:96339.text: Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle. A parcel addressed to you waited in a caretaker’s hands until you came to claim it. Inside was a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle, left by a courier whose name is unknown. The caretaker kept nothing in storage and had no wish to hold the parcel. The courier insisted you would come for it, then hurried away before the caretaker could refuse. You arrived just before the box was cast into the ocean with the evening’s refuse. Inside the parcel is a Replica Ironforge Air Rifle, a tribute to the firearm craft of the dwarven capital. Dwarven mountaineers and marksmen carry deadly weapons through Dun Morogh. Replicas like this recall the intricate barrelwork and pneumatic mechanisms perfected by Ironforge craftsmen.

quest:96604.text: The Great Outdoors. Brakk welcomes travelers beside his Basic Campfire and teaches them to rest in the wild. From there, they turn to practical crafts. Brakk greets aspiring adventurers with a hearty “Lok-tar” and welcomes those seeking fortune and glory. The road through Azeroth’s wilds asks for more than skill at arms; travelers must also endure the elements. Learning to make camp and regain strength is a first step toward surviving out there. Rest beside Brakk’s Basic Campfire brings a restorative pause in the open air and teaches travelers how to recover. Once they know these basics, novice adventurers can visit craftsmen in a nearby village. There, they can study tradeskills and learn to build camp fixtures suited to their chosen craft.

quest:96605.text: The Great Outdoors. At Kaga's wilderness camp, newcomers learn how to rest and recover. From the campfire, they go on to nearby artisans to learn tradeskills and craft camp fixtures. Kaga shows newcomers how to endure the wilderness beyond civilization. Courage alone cannot keep you safe there. You also need to know how to make camp and withstand the open elements. Kaga's campfire gives weary travelers a place to rest. Sit beside it to gain the Boosted Rest buff. Once you know how to rest in the wilds, Kaga urges you to visit artisans in a nearby settlement. They can teach you tradeskills and how to craft camp fixtures.

quest:96606.text: The Great Outdoors. At Lyreena's campfire, hunters learn how to rest before traveling through the wilds. They can gain the Boosted Rest buff there. Lyreena is an experienced scout who guides hunters beyond civilization's borders. She welcomes you to rest beside her campfire between hunts. In Azeroth's wilds, knowing how to make camp and regain your strength matters as much as tracking quarry. A campfire offers warmth and a quiet rest from travel. Sit near the flames to gain Boosted Rest and recover energy for the journey ahead. Rest helps you survive in the wilderness.

quest:96607.text: The Great Outdoors. Beyond city walls, The Great Outdoors teaches you to meet the wild with care. Seasoned travelers begin with a campfire and the habits that make each journey safer. A sharp blade or potent magic will not save you if you neglect the basics. Near roadside clearings, seasoned wanderers teach travelers leaving their home valleys to rest by a campfire. Its warmth eases sore boots, settles the mind, and prepares you for the harsh road ahead. Rest and preparation improve your chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory. Your instructors also send you to town tradesfolk, because a field camp needs more than an ember and a bedroll. You can forge replacement rivets, cook trail rations, or stitch torn gear beneath the stars. Each profession offers camp fixtures that help turn a bare hillside into a self-sufficient outpost.

quest:96608.text: The Great Outdoors. Eric waits by his campfire to teach travelers how to rest in the wild. Beyond settled places, ambition and a weapon or holy symbol are not enough. You need to know how to rest amid the elements. Eric has traveled far, and he welcomes you beside his campfire. There, he teaches why proper rest matters before you face the wilds. A campfire begins a useful campsite for a long journey. Once you have learned how to recover in the wild, visit tradeskill trainers in nearby settlements. They can teach you to make camp fixtures for your trade. Then your craft can support your travels wherever the road leads.

quest:96626.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In Goldshire, Cook Tomas shows new travelers how cooking kindles a campfire. With that fire, they can make a simple camp in the wild. A campfire gives you a place to prepare food and begin a camp in Azeroth's wilds. Learn to cook, and you learn to build that fire. Then an open stretch of wilderness can become a place to camp. In Elwynn Forest, new travelers find Cook Tomas in Goldshire and learn the craft. His instruction gives you the skill to make a basic camp in the wild. At first, your camp holds few furnishings. Greater cooking skill lets you build larger fires, while other crafting trades give you more ways to furnish and shape your campsite.

quest:96627.text: The Adventurer. From Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends you toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have proved your skill defending the abbey, and now he wants you to look into a newcomer. With the Defias and vermin threats easing, McBride turns his attention to the road beyond the valley. His garrison needs promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods. Marshal McBride asks you to check on Sam Sarsaparilla, who was spotted near Goldshire. This is neither a military order nor a hunt for a bounty. The newcomer draws you from Northshire’s secluded valley into Elwynn’s wider wilds.

quest:96628.text: The Adventurer. At Dun Morogh’s southern gate, The Adventurer carries supplies toward Kharanos. Mountaineer Thalos asks travelers to bring provisions to Eric Brighthammer, a newcomer camped just outside the village. Mountaineer Thalos keeps watch at Dun Morogh’s southern gate, where the trail leaves Coldridge Valley. Guarding the high passes and tunnels keeps the Mountaineers busy. Thalos also watches for dangers and travelers on the road. When a lone adventurer arrives near Kharanos, he asks trusted passersby to carry supplies onward. The bundle is meant to help newcomers venturing into the frozen crags. The road from the southern pass winds down to Kharanos, a center of dwarven craft and travel in central Dun Morogh. Eric Brighthammer has recently made camp just outside the village. Carrying the Mountaineers’ provisions to him links the sentries on the ridge with those walking the wilderness.

quest:96629.text: Camping 101: Cooking. In Dun Morogh, travelers learn to cook and make a fire for the wilds. Gremlock Pilsnor teaches novice adventurers in Kharanos. Cooking keeps food ready for the road and helps travelers light campfires at wilderness campsites. Your first camp in Dun Morogh begins with a fire. In Kharanos, Gremlock Pilsnor teaches novice adventurers to cook. The skill keeps food ready for the road. A sturdy campfire gives an outdoor camp its center. Once you can build a campfire, you can pitch a humble camp in the open wilderness. A simple fire holds only a few furnishings, but greater cooking skill lets you build larger blazes.
